Presence is also the **only side-effect-free probe available** — testing visibility would mean running every step's `reveal()`, which in the dictionary opens the sidebar and expands panels the tour hasn't reached (the exact artifact this pass's own first probe hit). The step being shown always counts itself, so torah's `_tourHoldForReading` (parked on a step whose target hasn't rendered) still numbers correctly. **torah `1,2,3,6 of 6` → `1,2,3,4 of 4`; dictionary `1,2,3,4,6,7 of 7` → `1..6 of 6`; both unchanged when the content loads.** Verified 12/12 matrix cells (light/dark × 1280/800 × three states): no jump, stable total, walk ends exactly at that total, 0 pageerrors, 0 vacuous runs; the 5 untouched tours unchanged.

The remedy the message offered ("edit the nodes or re-trace to fix") was not even available for a glyph nobody drew. The overlap loop now skips a pair **only when both contours are outer**; **outer/hole and hole/hole overlaps — the cases that actually cancel a region — still fire** (hole/hole was added deliberately: two overlapping counters double-subtract and invert, so "windings differ" alone would have been a narrower rule than correctness allows). A permanent unclearable warning is how a teacher learns to **ignore the panel that also carries the real findings about her own letters**. | verified headless light+dark × 1280/800, pageerror==0, 44 checks: untouched project raises **0** outline warnings and the QA panel keeps its placement verdict; **positive controls** confirm outer+hole and hole+hole still flag, self-intersection still detected (its call signature changed), normal counters + disjoint contours still clear, and a contour with **no** `winding` field still defaults to outer.

The app's own `_ivOpenFontsDB` then calls `indexedDB.open(IV_FONTS_DB, 1)`, finds an existing v1 database, gets **no upgrade event**, and every `db.transaction('fonts')` throws `NotFoundError`. At S308 this made "Use in IvritSuite" fail in all 4 cells with the page's genuine `resources.fonts.toast_add_error` — *"Sorry — couldn't add that font"* — on a feature S307 had shipped the session before. It reads as a shipped P1 regression, not as a probe artifact, which is exactly why it is worth writing down. **The tell:** the failure is total and identical in every cell, and the underlying steps pass when run directly (`fetch` 200, 12,608 bytes, `saveUserFont OK`). **The rule:** any virgin-state read of IndexedDB must be non-destructive — check `indexedDB.databases()` for the name first and return `'ABSENT'`, or open with the SAME version and the SAME `onupgradeneeded` the app uses. This sits with the S294 control rule, the S295 control-diagnosis refinement, the S297 handle rule and the S307 `page.evaluate`/forced-GC rules. | found: 2026-09-01, S308 Pass I

- [ ] P4 (**NEW S247 Pass M** — a probe DEFECT that produced three false findings before it was caught; recorded because every future M/C contrast probe inherits it) | pass M / pass C protocol | **A contrast probe must exclude disabled controls and composite element `opacity`.** S247's first run flagged `#regenBtn`/`#printBtn`/`#pdfBtn` at 1.84:1 — all three carry `disabled` + `aria-disabled="true"`, and **WCAG 1.4.3 explicitly exempts inactive user-interface components**. Exclude via `el.closest('[disabled],[aria-disabled="true"]')`. Separately, cumulative ancestor `opacity` must multiply into the foreground alpha or a dimmed control reads as full-strength. **And the inverse trap:** the generator's dark disabled treatment (`opacity:1` + explicit `#3d4f6a`) is deliberate and MORE legible than light's `opacity:0.35` — so the naive probe was not merely noisy, it was pointing at the better of the two implementations.

- [ ] P4 (**NEW S247 Pass M** — a METHOD finding; the arithmetic and the pixels disagreed and the pixels were right) | pass M protocol | **`getComputedStyle` cannot see a `filter`, and `brightness()` scales the TEXT as well as the background.** Predicting a filtered hover's contrast by brightening only the background gave 6.04:1 where the rendered pixels measure 5.86:1. Any fix delivered via `filter` (the suite's dominant gold-button hover idiom, 7 carriers) must be verified by **sampling rendered pixels** — decode the screenshot and take the background as the modal colour and the ink as the pixel furthest from it in luminance. Taking the *darkest* pixel as the ink silently reports 1.00:1 when the label is lighter than its field, which is exactly the failing case.

Fixing it means skipping contour-less `cat:'punct'` entries in pass 1 **and** in `emitBaseAnchors`' `LETTERS` loop in lockstep: that loop calls `seedAnchorsIfNeeded`, so a glyph dropped from `glyphOrder` would still get `pos base` lines and **feaLib would reject the whole FEA**. Adding them WITHOUT the pass-1 fix would ship 21 more blank glyphs and make `@` render as nothing — which is why v5.18 shipped letters only.

_(**S190 Pass L** — SEO & discoverability, **5th run**, taken on the S189 pointer's explicit instruction not to defer it a second time. The pointer's method worked exactly as designed: the **byte check ran FIRST** and cleared the copy dimensions in one command (`git diff -U0 1dcd2d7..HEAD -- ':(top)*.html'` → **0 changed lines** matching `<title>`/`name="description"`/`rel="canonical"`/`og:`/`twitter:`/`ld+json`, across **3,538 insertions in 7 root HTML files**), freeing the whole pass to converge on the dimensions that CAN have moved. **Structurally CLEAN for the 5th consecutive run:** canonicals 11/11 with the bare-root homepage; 404/i18n-test noindex + sitemap-absent (**and 404's canonical is still gone — the S174 finding fixed in S175 has not regressed**); sitemap↔canonical **exact 11/11 both directions**; 11/11 `<lastmod>` present; robots.txt Sitemap-directive intent correct with no blanket disallow; **35 JSON-LD blocks parse**; both og/twitter images (`og-card.png`, `og-fontmaker.png`) resolve on disk; titles+descriptions unique with sane lengths (titles 27–61, descriptions 92–164); **exactly one `<h1>` on all 13 pages**; **0 `<img>` without `alt`**; and the **crawl-graph 11/11 reachable from the homepage** (10 direct links, 0 pageerror across the crawl, and the crawl reached nothing outside the indexable set).

**The one dimension a byte check cannot clear produced all 3 findings — "do the claims still match what the tool does".** The copy is byte-identical; the UI beneath it moved 3,538 lines. All three were gate-2 approved and **all three shipped this session** (3237da8): FM's HowTo naming 3 of the wizard's 4 sources (Drawing mode absent) under a step still called "Upload your letters"; the dashboard's Schedule Sync answer describing "a preset and an end time to each period" — precisely the single-day format the tool now calls "your existing schedule" and offers to migrate into the weekly grid; and the dictionary's filter list omitting Browse by Theme.

**The scope discovery that mattered:** each JSON-LD claim has a **VISIBLE FAQ twin** on the same page, and every twin carried the *identical* stale wording in **both languages** — so the structured data was never diverging from the page; the page had fallen behind the tool. Fixing only the JSON-LD would have manufactured a fresh JSON-LD↔visible mismatch, worse than either, so both halves moved together (3 JSON-LD claims + 3 localized EN/HE strings, worded to agree).

**⚑ This REVISES a convention S142's L run ratified.** That run saw the same shape and wrote "newer features like dictionary themes / torah copy simply aren't enumerated, nothing claimed is stale" — i.e. non-enumeration is not staleness. S190 narrows it: a **closed enumeration that asserts the complete set** ("one per image, a full sheet, or an existing font file") IS stale once the set grows, and a description of *how a feature works* that no longer describes it (the dashboard) was never non-enumeration at all. Merely incomplete prose still isn't a hit. The dictionary item is the one S142 explicitly declined; it shipped this time because the maintainer chose all three at gate 2.

**Two would-be findings were KILLED by grounding before either was logged.** (1) og:title/og:description differ from twitter:title/twitter:description on **9 of 11 pages** — **not drift**: every tool page deliberately ships a shorter, brand-suffixed X variant (`Hebrew Flash Cards | IvritSuite`), with 9/11 twitter descriptions shorter than their og twin by design. My equality assertion was stricter than the property the site guarantees and failed 9 correct pages; the real contract (og set complete, `og:url === canonical`, `twitter:image === og:image`, `twitter:card` large) passes 11/11. (2) `404.html` reported a missing canonical as a FAIL — **already fixed in S175** (1c567d4); my diff window simply began after that commit. Both are now regression guards instead of findings.)_

_(**S189 Pass F** — cross-tool consistency, 16th run. Affordance: **busy / loading feedback during a slow operation** — never swept in 15 prior F runs (destructive resets S176, transient toasts S111/S155, share links S133, fullscreen + dark toggles S123, shared-block byte-identity S144/S154, font pickers S80/S100, tour pulses S90, empty states S71). Contract fixed BEFORE measuring, five dimensions: **PRESENT** (visible in-flight text) · **ANNOUNCED** (in a live region) · **CLEARS-OK** · **CLEARS-FAIL** (replaced by an error, never left as "Loading…") · **GUARDED** (no stacked re-fire). Method: each tool's own primary slow resource stalled 2.6–3.0 s and, separately, 502'd; sampled mid-flight and after settle; local HTTP, `serviceWorkers:'block'`.

**Five of seven tools PASS on every dimension:** torah_trainer (`#ttStatus` holds "Loading <label>…" for the whole 2.6 s window, `role=status aria-live=polite`, error line on 502, `_readingLoading`/`_fetchSeq` re-entrancy guard), trope_tutor (`#tuStatus`), font_maker (the most elaborate in the suite — engine badge + phased export-button label + sticky `#statusMsg` + a localized `askModal` on failure), dictionary (visible download progress in KB and %), dashboard (a per-widget line that correctly becomes "Weather unavailable"). **Two laggards; all four findings fixed this session** — see Done.

**Two candidate findings were KILLED by grounding before either was logged.** (1) font_maker's `#statusMsg` appeared to be stuck at "Loading font engine (one-time ~8 MB)…" permanently after a failure — **REFUTED at the reachable path**: all three foreground callers (`exportFont`, `generatePreviewPDF`, `offerSaveToMyFonts`) do `status('')` and then raise a localized error modal, and the background prefetch writes no status at all; my probe had called `ensurePyodide()` with no caller. (2) torah_trainer appeared to show **no** busy text — **a harness fault**: a `waitForFunction` on `#ttParshaSelect option` (that select has no direct `option` children) burned the entire in-flight window before the first sample.

**Informational, deliberately NOT logged as a convergence:** `aria-busy` appears in **0 of 9** files suite-wide. F's own rule treats a uniform absence as enhancement-to-all rather than a laggard, and every carrier already announces through `role="status"`, so `aria-busy` would add nothing.)_

_(**S191 Pass C** — accessibility, one tool: **`torah_trainer.html`**, the S190 pointer's strongly-favored target and its 4th dedicated C (S18 → S72 → S146 → S191). The point of the pick was the three interactive surfaces added since S146 that had never had a dedicated audit — the S190 sticky bulk dock, the S188 type-a-range verse picker, the copy bar — and **the pick paid: 2 of the 3 findings that shipped were defects in the bulk dock itself, one of them a P2.** Structurally the page remains very strong: 124 visible controls with 0 naming defects in either language, 64-stop tab order in a sensible region sequence, a clean drawer focus-trap/Escape/restore contract, 20/20 visible focus rings in both themes, 0 pageerrors everywhere.)_

**The method lesson of the run: the two loudest automated signals were both wrong, and both would have been logged by a less suspicious pass.** (1) "35 of 64 tab stops have no focus indicator" — Chromium computes its own UA focus ring as `outline: <color> auto 0px`, so **`getComputedStyle().outlineWidth` cannot detect a focus ring at all**; a screenshot pixel-diff refuted it 20/20 in both themes. Any future C run that reads styles for this is measuring nothing. (2) "6 tab stops are invisible (0×0)" — those are the toggle-switch `<input>`s, deliberately hidden behind their `.slider`, which the existing `input:focus-visible + .slider` rule rings correctly. **A third near-miss on the verification side:** the fix-verification harness reported the gold **Copy All** button at 1:1 because an opaque `rgb()` parses to 3 components, so an `alpha > 0` guard is `false` for it and every solid-background element gets measured against its ancestor's plate instead of its own fill. The guard must be `alpha === undefined || alpha > 0`.

**And the injection lesson, which cost the first three probe runs:** `currentVerses` is a top-level `let` in a non-module inline script, so it lives in the global **lexical** environment and is **not** a `window` property. `window.currentVerses = …` silently creates a shadowed twin — the harness reported the reading as rendered while `.tt-word` count was 0. A **bare assignment** is the only way in, and `injectReading` now throws on a 0-word receipt rather than proceeding.

Measured (S184 Pass D, `#ttReading.innerHTML` setter instrumented, 146 verses, everything on, TWO separate process runs): exactly 2 reading writes both runs — write 1 at t=152/166 ms, 403 KB, 0 translit rows, chip present; write 2 at t=286/309 ms, 498 KB, 146 translit rows, chip gone; gap between paints 134/143 ms at cpu 1 (the profiling agent measured the same shape at 179–412 ms, and 1.4–1.6 s at cpu 4). - [x] ✅ DONE S181, ce1eab2 | torah_trainer.html | **A4 paper silently discards every Hebrew font-size choice — the handout's three presets AND the teacher's font slider** (S181 Pass G; found INDEPENDENTLY by 3 of 4 surfaces plus my own measurement, then adversarially CONFIRMED with glyph sizes read out of the PDF content streams via PyMuPDF — not print-media emulation). `@media (max-width: 720px)` (~line 1061) is unqualified, so it applies to **print**, and its `.tt-cell.heb, .tt-heb { font-size:1.35rem }` is a literal at the same specificity as the `font-size:var(--tt-heb-size,1.5rem)` base rules (~411/616) but later in source order — so it beats both `applyFontSizes()`'s documentElement var and the handout's `body.tt-handout-size-large/-xl` body override. A4 at Chrome's default margins is 716.9–718.1px, under the 720px breakpoint; Letter at default is 740px and escapes. **Verifier widened it twice:** it fires **unconditionally** (even at the untouched 1.5rem default, A4 prints 1.35rem), and it is **width-driven, not paper-driven** — `A4@none` (794px) prints correctly while `Letter@0.5in` (720px) prints wrong, so US teachers who pick ½-inch margins are hit too. Receipts: handout large/xl = 35.2/44.8px on Letter vs **21.6px on A4**; PDF page counts Letter 2/3/5 vs A4 2/2/2. Severity corrected P1→P2 by the verifier. Page view is immune (`.tt-bible-heb` is not in the mobile rule). **Fix chosen against BOTH agents' recommendation, on measurement:** they proposed `@media screen and (max-width:720px)`; measured on paper that also hands A4 the 24px desktop `.tt-page` padding, shrinking its text column to 670px — 24px narrower than today and 22px narrower than Letter's 692px. Today's narrower mobile padding accidentally compensates for A4's narrower paper (694 vs 692). Restating the var chain inside the print block keeps that and is exactly what the file's S30 end-of-stylesheet source-order convention exists to enable.

- [~] Item (4) ✅ DONE 2026-07-29 (out-of-band, user-directed), b158af4; item (3) remains informational-only | torah_trainer.html | **Pass G print residuals** (S53). **(4) FIXED — side-by-side prints as parallel columns again.** S53 had collapsed it to one column because the two independent block flows broke at different points and produced **wrong verse pairings** (~15 verses out of sync) — truthful, but it cost the parallel text this layout exists for. Restored without the risk: in `@media print` the column wrappers become **`display:contents`** so every cell is a direct grid item, and the builder assigns each cell an **explicit `grid-row` shared across columns**, pinning a verse's Hebrew/translit/translation to the same row so they cannot drift wherever the page breaks. **The trap that made this non-trivial:** the Hebrew column also emits **aliyah dividers**, so it has more children than its siblings and any naive row-index alignment skews — the row map allocates a row per divider (spanning all columns). With no second text there is nothing to align, so that case keeps the single-column collapse rather than reserving an empty half-page. Screen is untouched (`grid-row`/`grid-column` are inert on non-grid-items; measured screen `grid-template-columns` identical before/after). **Method worth reusing: a standalone feasibility probe ran FIRST** — a throwaway page proving Chrome fragments an explicit-placement grid correctly (60 pairs, 4 pages, none split), which de-risked the whole change before a line of production code was written. Then a **negative control** (pre-fix 70/70 rows misaligned + 1 print column → post-fix 0/70 + 3 columns) and a 10-run × light/dark matrix covering 3-col, 2-col, no-parallel, interlinear and bible page; 12-page PDF generated and the rendered page inspected. **(3) still open, and still has no fix:** nikkud letter-mode colours print but collapse to similar greys on B/W — there is no secondary channel available for vowels the way the trope layer got its print underline.

  **Two maintainer decisions taken at build time:** ‹/› do BOTH (scroll between dividers on a full parsha; step the Reading picker + re-fetch on a single aliyah; aria-disabled with a stated reason elsewhere), and the bar AUTO-HIDES after 4 s idle rather than sitting permanently dimmed. **The seed's own pointer was already satisfied** — S180's `b7b7b7a` had removed the literal `font-size` from the `body.fullscreen` block, so A−/A+ move `--tt-heb-size` and work; the block's comment says never to re-add it. **Three extractions paid for ~a quarter of the diff**: `syncDarkButtons` (one loop, three carriers, replacing the same two lines copied per button across `toggleDark`+`initDark`, and guarding the header read that was unguarded); `FONT_SIZE_UI` + `setFontSize` (one slider map where there were THREE copies — `resetFontSize`, `syncFormToSettings`' `sizeMap`, the `wireSize` call list — and one writer for a size whatever drives it, clamping from the slider's own `min`/`max` so the bar can never leave the drawer's range); and `aliyahNumForLabel` lifted out of `updateJumpNavState`. **⚑ The bug verification caught, and the lesson:** stepping from `aliyahNumForLabel(_currentVerseLabel)` looked obviously right and was wrong — `jumpToAliyah` CENTRES the divider and the IntersectionObserver then reports the verse just ABOVE it (jump to aliyah 2, `_currentVerseLabel` reads `2:3`), so `›` recomputed the same target forever and could never pass the first divider. A single-press assertion would have passed; the **per-press walk of the whole cycle** (`[1,2,3,4,5,6,6,6,6]`) is what exposed it. Fixed with `fsAliyahIndexAtViewport()`, which reads the dividers' own positions — the section question, not the verse question. **Native `requestFullscreen()` WAS granted headless** (contrary to the plan's assumption), so the `fullscreenchange` listener, the Escape-exit focus rescue and the `#fsExitBtn` round-trip are covered for real, not simulated. Other notable arms: a faded bar does not intercept clicks over the reading (`elementFromPoint` returns a `.tt-word` across the strip — the `pointer-events` split is load-bearing, the wrapper spans `inset-inline:0`); zero extra Sefaria calls on a full-parsha step and exactly one per scope step; `data-twi` byte-identical across a step; `window.alert` never called; the disabled reason survives a language switch (the `applyI18n` re-assert); the bar clears `#fsExitBtn`, `.tt-jumpnav`, the karaoke bar and the hint toast at 1920 and 1280 with karaoke both on and off; `A−`/`A+` needed `dir="ltr"` on the glyphs alone (the sign is bidi-neutral and reordered to `−A` in the Hebrew UI) while the buttons still mirror.

### from Pattern health (per recurring pattern: last swept, hits that sweep, consecutive clean sweeps; detail in the sweep log below)

- **`elevation-cue-doubled-or-dead`**: **re-swept 2026-09-02 (S311 Pass O, `Hebrew_Font_Maker.html` help popup) — hits: 14, ALL FIXED. Clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE.** Two shapes this sweep, and the second is the more interesting: **(a) 4 DEAD SELECTION CUES** (`0c86195`) — `.mode-btn`/`.wtab`/`.ctab`/`.help-tab` fill with `var(--navy)`, which dark mode never redefines, so a chip at 14.00:1 in light read at **1.03–1.15:1** in dark. This is the registered "dead in the theme it is used in" inverse applied to *selection* rather than *elevation*, and it was found by censusing the file for siblings of a known-good rule (the `sibling-page-missing-a-shared-declaration` method, applied WITHIN one file). **(b) the 10 remaining hairline carriers** (`88f4940`), completing S309/S310. **⚑ DETECTION CAVEAT, HARDENED AGAIN:** the rule id is unreliable as a **counter** as well as a locator — ground truth 10 vs the static arm's 0 on flash_cards and 2 on resources. **⚑ AND ITS THRESHOLD IS EXACTLY 16px** (measured: clean 8–15, flagged 16–28), so the approved `0 6px 16px` treatment still fires; that is a ratified design choice, NOT a cleared tell — never record it as one. _(prior: re-swept 2026-09-02 (S310) — hits: 7, ALL FIXED (`21d0067`).)_ The 7 were the token-delivered carriers the S309 literal sweep could not see, exactly as the sibling `false-clean-from-a-literal-only-pattern-match` pattern predicted. **Detection refinement added S310:** the Impeccable rule id `gpt-thin-border-wide-shadow` is a PROMPT TO LOOK, NEVER A LOCATOR — it emits a phantom "28px" finding on pages with no such shadow (two proofs in Candidates). Count only from the token-aware `css-tree` scan plus a live DOM probe **with a passing firing control**. **Resolution rule, now settled by the maintainer:** the hairline STAYS and the shadow steps down the page's own token ladder (`--shadow-lg` → `--shadow-md`), rather than the reverse. **⚑ 10 elements from S309 still carry the OPPOSITE resolution** — see the open Candidate.

- **`false-clean-from-a-literal-only-pattern-match`** (**NEW, registered 2026-09-01 (S309 Pass O) — 1 carrier, and it had ALREADY been reported to the maintainer as a completed clean sweep before it was caught. ACTIVE — consequence-critical (it manufactures false assurance), so it does NOT retire on a clean streak**): a sweep whose detector matches only the **literal** form of a value and is therefore structurally blind to the same value delivered through an indirection — here `box-shadow: var(--shadow-lg)`, which a grep for `0 12px 32px` cannot see and which the Impeccable static arm also under-reports. Sibling of `false-clean-from-an-unverified-probe-handle` (S297) but a distinct shape: there the *handle* never resolved; here the handle resolved fine and the **filter** could not express the target. **Detection:** whenever a sweep's finder is a regex or a literal string match over CSS/JS values, ask what the same value looks like behind a custom property, a helper function, a constant, or a class — then re-run through a real parser (S309 used `css-tree` from the detector's own `node_modules`, resolving `var()` recursively). **Exemption:** none. **Standing rule this registers:** a "0 remaining" claim from a literal matcher is a claim about the *matcher*, not about the code, and must be labelled that way when reported.

- **`elevation-cue-doubled-or-dead`** (**NEW, registered 2026-09-01 (S309 Pass O) — 14 literal carriers found and fixed across 8 files (`e9ac7a4`, `2d0a170`), 7 more found by a token-aware re-scan and DEFERRED to S310 by the maintainer, and 3 pages whose dark-mode shadow was invisible fixed in `3333d60`. ACTIVE**): a surface that hedges between two separation cues — a 1px hairline border *and* a wide soft shadow — instead of committing to one; and its inverse, a shadow token that is dead on the theme it is used in. Impeccable calls the first `gpt-thin-border-wide-shadow` and rates it among the most recognizable AI-UI tells. **Detection:** `node "$DET" --json <page>` for the rule id, PLUS the token-aware `css-tree` scan (both a grep and the detector's static arm miss `var()`-delivered shadows), PLUS — for the dead-shadow inverse — compositing the dark-block shadow colour over that page's `--cream` and checking the max channel delta (under ~5/255 is invisible). **The fix is never one recipe:** drop the border only where the element floats over a dimming backdrop; keep it and tighten the shadow where it is load-bearing (a dropdown with no backdrop, a frosted-glass rim, a drag-resize seam). **Exemptions:** none registered yet; the three `.settings-modal` drawers are open questions, not exemptions.

- **`sibling-page-missing-a-shared-declaration`** (**NEW, registered 2026-08-31 (S304 Pass M) — 3 carriers found and fixed in one commit**): several pages render the *same* markup (a shared header/footer element, a chrome component) but one or more of them omit a declaration the others carry, so a value silently falls back to an inherited one and that page alone looks wrong — **invisible to any single-page audit, because on one page the fallback usually looks deliberate**. **Detection:** pick an element class that appears on multiple pages, census its COMPUTED value across every carrier in both themes, then confirm at source that the divergent pages *lack the declaration* rather than overriding it on purpose. A hit needs both. **Always widen to every carrier before filing** — the S262 measure-the-token-everywhere rule is what turns "3 pages are wrong" into "9 of 12 set it, 3 do not". **Fix shape:** add the missing declaration only; verify any *other* declaration the correct carriers share is actually load-bearing before copying it too (S304 measured `flex-shrink:0` INERT and deliberately left it out). **Prior instances, recognised retroactively:** S246's `.hright{display:flex}` missing on index+404 and its `.hbtn` 27px — same shape, same chrome family, not registered at the time. **Carriers fixed:** privacy/terms/contact's white brand star (`e093389`). Swept 2026-08-31, hits: 3, clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE.

- **`panel-collapse-writer-mismatch`** (**NEW, registered 2026-08-31 (S303) — swept across all 6 panel-collapse carriers; 4 hits in 3 files, ALL FIXED; 2 carriers clean. ACTIVE**): a **bulk** writer of the `.collapsed` class that disagrees with the panel-collapse memory's contract, in **either** direction. Shape **(a)**, the one CLAUDE.md names: a user-intent bulk writer (Expand-all / Collapse-all) that does NOT call `panelMemSave()`, so a deliberate tidy is forgotten — found in `hebrew_dictionary`, `hebrew_blend_generator`, `classroom_dashboard` (6 functions, one missing call each); `torah_trainer` and `flash_cards` were already correct and served as the firing controls. Shape **(b)**, the inverse and the one a naive reading of that rule would CREATE: a **layout-driven** writer whose collapse is an adaptation, not a choice, and which must therefore never be persisted — found once, `hebrew_dictionary`'s `enterMobile()`, where it was rewriting the teacher's desktop layout from their phone. **Detection:** `grep -n "classList.add('collapsed')" ` over the six carriers, then read each writer and ask *who* decided — a person or a viewport. Tour restore paths (`_tourUncollapsed`) are exempt by the read-only tour contract. **The pattern exists because the constitution's own wording ("call `panelMemSave()` from every writer of `.collapsed`") is right for (a) and wrong for (b);** a future sweep must classify, not just count.

- **`false-clean-from-an-unverified-probe-handle`**: **FOUR MORE ARTIFACTS at 2026-08-31 (S300), all caught before any verdict was filed — the pattern is now four-for-four and remains the loop's most valuable registered pattern. ACTIVE (method pattern; never retires).** S300's four, all in the session's OWN probes: **(1)** the shared-block sha census used the wrong end markers for two blocks (`═══ end .ivrit engine ═══` and `═══ end folder-tree component ═══` do not follow the `end shared: <name>` convention the other eleven use); both returned `NO-END-MARKER` with length 0 and the script still printed **"IDENTICAL"**, because all four carriers shared the same sentinel — *a clean verdict computed entirely from failure*. **(2)** a broken-link probe reported **16 broken links, all artifacts**: `/` scored missing because `os.path.exists('')` is false, and a loose `(?:href|src)=` regex matched `data-rwsrc="all"` and a JavaScript `src = 'imported'` assignment. **(3)** a manifest probe reported **132 of 132 partner fonts missing** — the `file` field already carries its directory prefix, so the join was doubled; **a 100% failure rate is itself the tell**. **(4)** the micro-feature's fresh-profile arm measured `localStorage.length` *after* `page.goto` and read the keys the page had just written, reporting a virgin context as dirty. **⚑ THE S300 LESSON, and it is a new one: the fired-control rule is necessary but NOT sufficient.** Artifact (1) had no control at all and would have shipped a false clean; artifacts (2) and (4) *did* fire — and fired **falsely positive**, which is the failure mode a control cannot catch, because a probe that reports something looks like a probe that works. **So the control answers "can it fire?", and only reading the actual reported items answers "is it right?" — never accept a count without eyeballing the items behind it.** Artifact (2)'s own pass/fail assertion was ALSO wrong (it expected exactly 1 hit and saw 2, declaring the passing control a failure), so even the control needs its assertion checked.

- **`invisible-rebuild-on-a-hot-render-path`**: **re-swept 2026-08-31 (S299 Pass A) — hits: 0. Clean streak: 1 — ACTIVE.** Swept on the exact four surfaces the S294 registration named as unswept (dashboard settings drawer, flash-cards setup, torah + trope drawers), by the registered definition. Two near-misses **measured and deliberately not filed**, both failing the definition's second leg (cost that scales with data): torah `updateCopyTextarea` is called **8/8 times while `#ttCopyTextarea` is hidden** on the display-toggle path but costs **0.24ms/call** at 60 verses — a single string assignment into a textarea `value`, no DOM construction; trope `updateDrillStart` rebuilds `masteryGridStart` **10/10 while hidden** at **0.46ms/call** over a **bounded** 26-trope inventory. Flash cards' `renderPresets`/`renderProfiles`/`renderEmojiCatTree` DO write hidden containers (18/18, 18/18, 11/11 mutations) **but only when forced** — their real callers are preset/profile CRUD and emoji-mode entry, not a hot path. **⚑ DETECTOR ADDENDUM (S299): the dashboard's renderers are NESTED functions, so the S294 approach of wrapping `window[fn]` silently instruments nothing and returns a false clean.** Use a **MutationObserver** on the target container instead — scope-independent, and it measured 0 mutations across 6s of idle clock ticks (the dashboard's hottest path, the clock, touches none of them).

- **`sub-floor touch target`**: **re-swept 2026-08-30 (S298 Pass C + iters 2–3) — hits: 13 visible tooltip triggers across 4 carriers, ALL FIXED** (`1206653` torah/trope/dashboard, `63cf248` generator). The badge painted 15×15 on every carrier — under the 24px floor, and the single smallest target on each page, which is perverse given it is the affordance the suite's tap-to-open tooltip contract exists to serve. Fixed with the **sanctioned second vehicle** (S240): a transparent `::after` raising the POINTER target to 25×25 with the paint untouched, so no settings row reflows. **⚑ THE DETECTOR MUST BE PSEUDO-AWARE OR IT LIES IN BOTH DIRECTIONS.** A `getBoundingClientRect` census (a) re-files every control S240-style remediation already fixed — the four torah per-verse chips read 62×19 but hit-test to 24px — and (b) cannot confirm a fix. Use `elementFromPoint` stepping out from the element's centre, and **guard it twice**: skip elements not fully in the viewport (badges inside a CLOSED drawer return null everywhere, making "no vehicle" and "off-screen" indistinguishable — this cost S298 a full round), and dismiss first-run backdrops (`#frBackdrop` on the dashboard) as well as `.overlay.open`. Tap-verification uses the `help-affordance-inside-a-label-forwards-its-tap` method: real coarse-pointer descriptor, **one fresh context per tap**, tap a point that exists ONLY inside the new vehicle (3px above the paint), and assert both that the bubble opened and that the labelled control did not change. Clean streak: 0 — **ACTIVE.**

- **`author-display-defeats-the-hidden-attribute`** (**NEW, registered 2026-08-30 (S297) — 1 carrier found and fixed, then the whole suite swept CLEAN**): an element carrying the `hidden` **attribute** whose CSS also sets a `display`. The UA stylesheet's `[hidden] { display:none }` is an author-beatable default, so any class rule that sets a display **silently un-hides the element** — it renders in full while every `.hidden` check in the JS still reports it as hidden. **The carrier:** S297's new `#tuRetryBtn` in `trope_tutor.html`, which carries `.btn-xs` (`display:inline-flex`) and therefore rendered a "↻ Try again" button on every **successful** load, offering a retry for a failure that had not happened. Caught by the fix's own control run, not by review. **This is a known trap the suite already documents twice** — `torah_trainer.html` carries `.tt-trope-legend[hidden] { display:none; }` with the comment *"display:flex would beat the hidden attr"*, and S296 added `.tt-key-hints[hidden]` for the same reason — which is exactly why it is worth registering: it has now been rediscovered three times, and the third time it shipped. **Fix idiom:** `#id[hidden]`/`.class[hidden] { display:none; }` beside the component's own rules. **Detector — RUNTIME, and do not weaken it to a static grep:** load the page and flag `[...document.querySelectorAll('[hidden]')].filter(e => e.getClientRects().length > 0)`. Client rects rather than `getComputedStyle(el).display !== 'none'`, because a hidden element nested inside a `display:none` ancestor still computes its own specified display and would report as a false carrier; an element with no layout boxes is genuinely not rendered. **Proven both directions (S297):** with the guard removed the detector names the button (`display=inline-flex text="↻ Try again"`), and with it restored it is silent. Swept 2026-08-30 (S297) — **108 `[hidden]` element instances across 13 pages × EN/HE, hits: 1 (the S297 carrier, fixed in the same commit), 0 pre-existing**; clean streak: 1 — **ACTIVE** (cheap to re-run, and new code reintroduces it every time someone gives a `hidden` element a flex/grid class).

- **`false-clean-from-an-unverified-probe-handle`** (**NEW, registered 2026-08-30 (S297) — FIVE carriers in a single session, all caught before any verdict was filed**): a verification probe that calls a function which does not exist, or queries a selector that matches nothing, and therefore **never runs the thing it claims to test**. It does not throw and it does not read as broken — it returns a clean, quiet, **falsely reassuring** result (a `✓`, a zero, a "SILENT" verdict). **That is why this is consequence-critical and stays ACTIVE regardless of streak: it is strictly worse than a false positive**, because a false positive gets investigated while a false clean silently closes a question the loop believes it asked, and the ledger then carries the answer forward as a receipt. **S297's five carriers:** `loadWords()` (flash-cards corpus-failure arm — the real name is `fetchAllWordsData`; the arm reported the tool "SILENT" on failure when it in fact shows a caption), `generateWorksheet()` (the real name is `generate()`; the interaction arm scored a `✓` on an interaction that never happened), `loadRealWordsPool()` (the real name is `ensureRealWords`; the retry arm reported "NONE VISIBLE"), an `index.html` gear selector matching nothing (`✓` on a modal that never opened — the real opener is `openIEModal()` revealing `#ieBackdrop`), and a `.heb` selector on the generator worksheet reporting **0 Hebrew cells** on a worksheet that actually held 40 `.blend-cell`s and 133 Hebrew characters. **Detector (three guards, weakest to strongest — use the third wherever the arm touches the network): (1)** `if (typeof fn !== 'function') return 'MISSING <fn>'` before calling; **(2)** assert `document.querySelector(sel)` is non-null before measuring it; **(3) count the side effect** — a `page.route` counter proving the request was actually attempted, which is what exposed three of the five (`data/ requests seen: 0` next to a "no failure message" verdict is the tell). **Relationship to the S294/S295 control rule:** that rule catches a detector that *cannot fire*; this one catches a detector that *never ran*. They are complementary and this family's instance count is now EIGHT across S295–S297 (S295's two probe artifacts, S296's grep matching its own CSS comment, S297's five). Swept 2026-08-30 (S297) — hits: 5, all diagnosed and re-run correctly, 0 false findings filed; clean streak: 0 — **ACTIVE**.

- **`ledger-section-loss`** (**NEW, registered 2026-08-30 (S296) — 1 carrier found and fixed, and a DETECTOR shipped with it**): a close-out edit that **deletes** ledger content instead of **moving** it to `docs/IMPROVEMENT_ARCHIVE.md`. The carrier: the S295 close-out (`be3eac8`) archived S290's five Done entries correctly and, in the same commit, removed **993 further lines / ~934 KB** that reached the archive nowhere — the entire `## Metrics` section (Per-session log, Tool coverage, **Pattern health**, Retired patterns), `## Recurring-pattern sweep status`, the **`### Discovery-pass rotation` table** and the historical `_(prior)_` pointer chain. Ledger 1,828 → 845 lines; archive +10. **Consequence-critical, so ACTIVE regardless of streak** (it is data loss, and the loss is self-concealing: the very sections that record what to sweep and what is stalest are the ones that vanish, so the next session cannot notice from the ledger alone — S296 found it only because a maintainer asked why the PR diff looked lopsided). **Cause is mechanical and will recur:** close-out archiving is a hand-written line-range edit and an end index past the Done section truncates everything after it. **Detector (run it; do not re-derive a weaker one): `node scripts/check-ledger.mjs --vs origin/main`** — check 1 asserts all 11 required section headings plus exactly one current `**Next session (SN):**` pointer; check 2 asserts bulk conservation (ledger shrinkage > 60 substantive lines must be matched by archive growth of at least half that). Deliberately bulk-based, not exact-line: candidates are rewritten in place constantly (striking one as done replaces its text), and an exact-line test reported that normal churn as loss. **Both checks were proven to fire against `be3eac8` itself** (7 sections named; "lost 888 substantive lines, archive gained only 5") and to pass on the repaired ledger. Swept 2026-08-30 (S296) — hits: 1, FIXED (restored byte-identical from `be3eac8^`); clean streak: 0 — **ACTIVE**.

- **`invisible-rebuild-on-a-hot-render-path`** (**NEW, registered 2026-08-30 (S294 Pass D) — 1 carrier found and fixed, and the same pass MEASURED the rest of the class closed on this page**): a render function on a hot path rebuilds a container that is `display:none` under the current view state, so the cost is paid on every state change and buys nothing — worst when the rebuilt list is **unbounded** (one DOM row per data item) rather than a fixed inventory. **Detection:** find the render entry point called on most state changes (here `renderGrids()`, 56 sites), list the containers it writes, and check each at runtime with `offsetParent !== null` / `getClientRects().length` under the DEFAULT view — not by reading CSS, since the hiding may come from an ancestor. A hit needs both *hidden by default* and *cost that scales with data*. **Fix shape:** guard the renderer on the view state and re-render from the single writer of that state (verify it IS single). **Carrier fixed:** FM `renderSpacingPanel`/`renderKerningSection` (`fa1f88f`). **Same-page census: the other nine cat-panel renderers total ~19ms at 4× and are bounded — deliberately NOT fixed** (P4 above). **Sweep next in:** the other tools' tabbed/collapsible panels — the dashboard drawer, flash-cards setup, torah/trope drawers — none swept. ACTIVE.

- **`mobile-input-hints`**: **re-swept 2026-08-30 (S292 iter 4) — hits: 1, FIXED** (`a393343`, `Hebrew_Font_Maker.html` `.guide-name`, closing the S290 Pass N arm-5 candidate — the file's one field with `spellcheck` but no `autocapitalize`/`autocorrect`; all three attribute sets now count 15). A **second** carrier was probed the same session and came back clean: `hebrew_dictionary.html` `#shoreshInput` already carries all three, checked because S292's own micro-feature routes `/` to it in Shoresh mode. Clean streak: **0** (a hit this sweep). **ACTIVE** — and the standing S255 caveat still governs any widening: "no hint" is not "defect", prose fields keep the sentence default, and a sweep treating the 42-field baseline as 42 bugs would ship 42 regressions.

- **`dark-mode-token-as-text-on-a-light-ground`** (**NEW, registered AND CLOSED 2026-08-29 (S291 iters 2+4) — 2 carriers found, both fixed, suite census clean**): a rule paints text with a token whose value is tuned for the OTHER theme's ground, so it is correct in one mode and unreadable in the other. Concretely: `var(--gold-light)` is the DARK-mode gold, and used unscoped it lands on the LIGHT cream ground at **1.41:1**. Carriers: `main a:hover` on contact/privacy/terms (`6a37029`) and `404`'s `.code-404 .lost-star` + numerals (`a71a329`). **Detection is one cheap grep** — enumerate every `color:var(--gold-light)` (and any future `--*-light` token used as text), then adjudicate each by its EFFECTIVE background: correct on `--navy` surfaces or under a `body.dark` scope, a hit on `--cream`/`--white`. **The suite-wide census at S291 found no third carrier**, which is why this registers as closed rather than open. **The fix shape is the reusable half:** do not copy the other theme's VALUE, mirror its RELATIONSHIP — the emphasis is brighter on dark and darker on light, and the 404 fix reproduced dark's 1.54× contrast ratio as light's 1.52×. **Re-check in A2**, not in every A: one grep, and a false positive is impossible to miss.

- **`non-finite-number-from-a-loaded-file`**: **2nd carrier FIXED 2026-08-29 (S287 iter 2, `5197b1e`) — the flash-cards half the S286 registration sweep found and filed. Hits this session: 1 carrier (6 fields). Clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE** (consequence-critical: a tab-freezing denial of service plus silent settings corruption). Both known carriers are now clamped — Font Maker at `migrateProject` (`sanitizeFontNumbers`, S286) and flash cards at `applySettings` (`_clampNum`/`_clampChoice`, S287). **Detector, restated from the S286 structural finding and CONFIRMED here: the question is not "does it parse untrusted JSON" but "does the number reach a consumer without passing through a form control"** — the generator and dashboard stay immune because `<input type=number>` rejects `Infinity` outright and `type=range` clamps. **S287 NARROWS THE REACH S286 CLAIMED:** an app-GENERATED share code cannot carry a non-finite value (`JSON.stringify` emits `null` for Infinity), so the vector is a hand-crafted `.ivrit`/share/`?s=` payload — `ivritSafeParse` is prototype-safe but does NO numeric validation. Next sweep should look for a third carrier of the same shape: a numeric held in a plain JS object and read straight by a loop or timer.

- **`non-finite-number-from-a-loaded-file`** (**NEW, registered 2026-08-29 (S286 iters 4–5) — 1 carrier fixed, a 2nd carrier + a P1 hang found and filed**): a numeric setting arriving from untrusted text — a `.hfm`/`.ivrit` file, an AllTools blob, a share code, a `?s=` param — reaching a build/render/export consumer **without ever being clamped**. **`1e999` is VALID JSON and parses to `Infinity`; `typeof Infinity === 'number'` and `Math.round`/`Math.max`/`Math.min` are all no-ops on non-finites**, so every `!= null` and `typeof === 'number'` guard in the suite passes it through. **Detection (the sweep method, and it is a RUNTIME one — nothing here is greppable):** take the tool's own `getSettings()`, poison every numeric key with `JSON.parse('1e999')`, push it through the tool's import chokepoint (`applySettings` / `migrateProject`), then read back and count non-finite survivors; time the call and treat a non-completion as a hang candidate to be re-probed from OUTSIDE the blocked thread. **⚑ The discriminator, and the thing that makes this cheap to triage: does the number pass through a FORM CONTROL on its way in?** `<input type=number>` rejects "Infinity" outright and `<input type=range>` clamps to its own min/max, so the generator (14 inputs) and dashboard (15 inputs) are **structurally immune** — 0 survivors each. The exposed tools are exactly those holding numerics in a **plain JS object read straight by a consumer**: the Font Maker (`project.font.*` → `buildFEA`, **FIXED** `6723c26`) and flash cards (**5 survivors + a P1 `mode` hang, FILED**). **⚑ Note the interaction with the loop's own ratified `??` rule:** nullish-coalescing is correct for falsy-zero and does nothing whatever for non-finites — `s.field ?? default` accepts `Infinity` happily. The two rules are complements, not substitutes. **swept 2026-08-29 (S286), hits: 2 carriers of 4 tools; clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE, consequence-critical (export corruption + a main-thread hang), never retires on streak.**

- **`var()-on-an-undefined-custom-property`**: **re-swept 2026-08-29 (S286 Pass A) — hits: 0. Clean streak: 1 — ACTIVE.** **⚑ THE DETECTOR IS NOW A RUNTIME ONE AND THE STATIC SUSPECT-GENERATOR IS RETIRED — do not go back to grepping.** S285 registered a static reader with a 46:1 false-positive rate; S286 hit **6 MORE false positives on `trope_tutor`** in a *third* spelling it could not see (`setProperty(\`--trope-${fam.key}-line\`, hex)` — a TEMPLATE LITERAL computed name, where S285 recorded string concat), all 12 consumer sites runtime-confirmed live in both themes. **The replacement walks the real CSSOM:** for every declaration whose value uses `var(--tok)` with NO fallback, match its selector and read the computed `--tok` on up to 4 matched elements — empty on all of them means the declaration is invalid at computed-value time and silently reverts to its INITIAL value. **1,317 (selector, prop, token) triples measured across 26 cells (13 pages × light/dark): 0 dead.** It has **zero** false positives (it measures the property rather than inferring it) and it closes the static reader's structural blind spot: a token that IS defined but on a **selector that does not match the consumer**. **⚑ Two probe traps, both hit and both fixed before any zero was believed:** (1) under CSS nesting a plain `CSSStyleRule` ALSO exposes an (empty) `.cssRules`, so an `if (r.cssRules) { recurse; continue; }` guard silently skips **every style rule on the page** — process `.style` FIRST, then recurse only when `.cssRules.length`; (2) the control must inject BOTH shapes (never-defined AND defined-out-of-scope) — it fired 4/4 only after the nesting fix, and reported a clean-looking 0 before it.

- **slider-focus-lost-to-its-own-rebuild**: **CLASS CLOSED 2026-08-29 (S286 iter 2) — the last 6 known carriers fixed (`9a01f3b`); hits: 6, clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE.** Registered S284 (3 fixed, 6 logged unreachable). All six routed through the shared re-focus helper (`udSliderCommit(id)`, plus a new `drawSliderCommit(id)` that keeps the draw panel's `drawSavePrefs()` write). **⚑ S284's recorded blocker was a WRONG DIAGNOSIS and cost a session: it said draw mode "needs a letter with contours". It does not — `_setWorkMode('draw')` gates on `project.inputMode !== 'draw'`, so `setInputMode('draw')` is the whole fixture.** Re-measured after the fix by the pattern's own method (real `ArrowRight`, one fresh context per slider): every fixed slider now steps repeatedly and holds focus, and draw mode's other 4 visible sliders were driven too — 0 lost. **A verification asymmetry recorded rather than hidden: 5 of the 6 were driven live; the Width slider's wide-form panel could not be surfaced headless and was fixed on the identical signature.**

- **class-only-selected-state**: **re-swept 2026-08-29 (S286 Pass A, suite-wide runtime) — hits: 0. Clean streak: 1 — ACTIVE.** Detector: any element carrying `.active`/`.selected`/`.current`/`.on` that is a control (button/link/`role`/`onclick`/tabbable), is visible, has **≥1 sibling sharing one of its non-state classes** (the group requirement that kills the noise), and carries none of `aria-pressed`/`aria-checked`/`aria-selected`/`aria-current`. **10 pages, 0 hits, detector proven able to fire** on an injected 2-button group. Covers the S283 meteg surface and the newly-reachable draw panel (whose `.brush-tile` group already carries `aria-pressed`).

- **animation-outside-its-reduced-motion-block**: **re-swept 2026-08-29 (S286 Pass A, all 13 pages at runtime) — hits: 0. Clean streak: 1 — ACTIVE.** Measured, never grepped, per the CLAUDE.md rule: `newContext({reducedMotion:'reduce'})` then count every element with a non-`none` `animationName` over 0.01s **and** every element with a non-zero `transitionDuration`. **All 13 pages: 0 animating and 0 transitioning under `reduce`**, and every zero is earned — the `reduce`-off control shows real activity (dictionary 684 transitions, generator 404, flash cards 217, dashboard 148). **⚑ `privacy.html` and `terms.html` read 0/0 in BOTH conditions, so their result is BLIND, not clean** — they declare no animation, exactly as CLAUDE.md documents; do not count them as coverage.

- **`var()-on-an-undefined-custom-property`** (**NEW, registered 2026-08-29 (S285 iters 3–4) — 1 carrier found suite-wide, fixed**): a declaration whose `var(--token)` has **no fallback** and whose token is never defined on that page is *invalid at computed-value time*, so the property reverts to its **initial** value — NOT to whatever the un-themed base rule set. Silent: no console error, no visual "missing" marker, and nothing to grep for, because the rule LOOKS correct. Detection: per file, collect `--token:` declarations plus `setProperty('--token'` literals, then every `var(--token)` reference with no fallback comma, and diff — **then CONFIRM each suspect at runtime**, because a token set from JS under a *computed* name (`setProperty('--nikv-' + key, …)`) is invisible to the static reader (46 such false positives on torah/trope, all resolving live; false-positive rate 46:1). Swept 2026-08-29 over all 14 root HTML files, hits: 1 (`hebrew_dictionary` `--navy-deep`, fixed `5e9a6d2`), clean streak: 0 — **ACTIVE**.

- **slider-focus-lost-to-its-own-rebuild** (**NEW, registered 2026-08-29 (S284 iter 3) — 3 carriers found and fixed, 6 more logged**): an `input[type=range]` whose `onchange` calls a function that rebuilds the panel containing it (`renderControls()` → `innerHTML` replacement) is DESTROYED by that rebuild, so focus falls to `<body>`. A mouse drag never notices (`change` fires once, on release, and the pointer holds its own target); an **arrow-key user gets exactly ONE step and every later press does nothing**. Detection: focus each visible range input and send real `ArrowRight` presses, asserting `document.activeElement` is still that slider after EACH press — a static grep for `onchange=.*renderControls` finds candidates but cannot tell you whether the container is actually rebuilt. Fix vehicle: `udSliderCommit(id)` (commit → rebuild → re-focus by id). Carriers fixed: `metegGapSlider`, `tropSpread`, `vowelPairDx`. **swept 2026-08-29, hits: 3, clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE.** Confined to `Hebrew_Font_Maker.html`: no other tool puts an `onchange` on a range input at all (0 across the other six), and 15 sliders driven live elsewhere all held focus.

- **help-affordance-inside-a-label-forwards-its-tap** (**NEW, registered 2026-08-29 (S284 iter 5) — 6 carriers in one file, all fixed**): a tooltip/help trigger placed INSIDE a `<label>` that wraps a form control inherits the label's activation forwarding, so one tap produces a second click on that control. Two consequences at once: the outside-click handler reads the forwarded click as "outside" and **hides the bubble that just opened**, and the control **silently changes state** — a teacher tapping "what does this do?" gets no answer and an unrequested setting change. `e.stopPropagation()` cannot cover it (it stops bubbling, not the default action); the fix is `e.preventDefault()` in the trigger's click handler. Detection: under a REAL coarse-pointer device descriptor with **one fresh context per tap** (sequential taps in one page contaminate each other — the first probe reported 2/4 and the isolated re-run 2/5), tap each trigger and assert BOTH that the bubble stays visible AND that the labelled control's value is unchanged; the giveaway on a failing tip is that `#tipFloat` still holds the RIGHT TEXT, proving `show()` ran and something hid it. **swept 2026-08-29, hits: 6, clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE, and consequence-critical (it mutates the teacher's saved settings), so it does NOT retire on streak.** Census: dictionary 6, torah 0, trope 0, dashboard 0, flash_cards 0.

Residual limit: a handler assembled from a string or bound inside dynamically-injected script would still escape static extraction.key` comparisons would be missed entirely.

- **fixed-control-positioned-outside-the-viewport**: **REGISTERED + first swept suite-wide 2026-08-26 (S262 Pass N) -- hits: 1 carrier (`hebrew_blend_generator.html` `#sidebarToggleBtn`), fixed in-pass (`5f6a0a0`); census 78 cells (13 pages x 3 phone descriptors x EN/HE) otherwise CLEAN; clean streak: 0 -- ACTIVE.** **Definition:** a `position: fixed` control whose inset is computed from a CONTAINER's edge (`el.style.left = rect.right`) rather than from the viewport, so at any layout where that container spans the full width the control lands wholly outside the visible area. **Why it needs its own pattern rather than living under `horizontal-overflow-at-narrow-widths`: a fixed element never contributes to `scrollWidth`, and it is not clipped by an `overflow:hidden` ancestor either** -- so it produces NEITHER overflow NOR clipping, and `scrollWidth <= innerWidth` (the reflow arm's whole assertion) reports CLEAN while the control is 100% unreachable. Confirm a hit with an `elementFromPoint` sweep across the row at the control's own vertical centre -- **and the probe MUST carry a control that returns non-zero taps, or a zero proves nothing** (S262's control: the viewport-pinned show-tab returned 12 taps in the same probe that returned 0 for the toggle; the detector itself was proved to fire 6/6 against the pre-fix file before the clean census was believed).

- **executable-javascript-in-a-localization-cell**: **REGISTERED 2026-08-26 (S261 Pass K) — swept the whole corpus, hits: 2 rows / 4 cells, all fixed in-pass (`ff1789e`); clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE, consequence-critical (security-shaped), never retires on streak.** **Definition:** a `locales/ui-strings.csv` cell whose value contains an inline event handler (`onclick=` &c.) or a `javascript:` URL, where the key is used at a `data-i18n-html` site — so `applyStaticI18n` writes executable markup into `innerHTML`. **Say the consequence honestly: this is NOT a live XSS.** The corpus is first-party and build-time, and CLAUDE.md sanctions `data-i18n-html` as "trusted CSV only". It is (a) a breach of Security rule 2's carve-out that an inline-handler site must be rebuilt with `addEventListener`, and (b) a translation-pipeline hazard — the CSV is the file a translator edits, and hand-authoring a new language column is a documented workflow (i18n §8), so a function name, a string argument and `return false;` end up inside the translatable payload where localizing them breaks a working control silently. **Detection is now AUTOMATED and needs no future hand-sweep: `check-i18n.js` Check C1**, blocking, column-driven. Regex is an explicit HTML event-attribute list, not a bare `on\w+=`, so prose cannot false-positive. **Fix shape:** a declarative `data-*` hook plus ONE DELEGATED listener — never a listener bound to the element, because `applyStaticI18n` rebuilds these nodes on every language switch (controlled: the node identity changes and a directly-bound listener fires 0 times afterwards).

Control earned before any verdict: run against `050a46f~1` it reports 8 shape-(a) mismatches, so the 6 S260 fixed are provably gone and these 2 are provably what its shape missed. **Post-fix state: 0 of 65 `data-i18n-html` sites and 0 of 1,756 plain `data-i18n` sites — the whole class is at zero for the first time.** shape (b) held clean on its own, confirming `97d272d`. **A THIRD SHAPE IS NAMED HERE: `stale-html-fallback-behind-its-csv-value`** — `adv_special_hint`'s fallback was a pre-v5.33 draft while the CSV carried the current text. It is the mirror of shape (a) (the fallback is behind, not ahead) and its consequence is confined to the pre-`I18n.ready` flash, so cosmetic — but the multiset detector catches it for free and it is a genuine content-drift signal. **Detection is now AUTOMATED: `check-i18n.js` Check C's markup-parity report** (warn-only) covers all three shapes; a future sweep reads the checker rather than re-deriving a probe.

- **i18n-html-markup-only-in-fallback**: **REGISTERED 2026-08-26 (S260) — swept suite-wide, hits: 21 across 4 tools, all fixed in-pass (`050a46f` 6, `97d272d` 15); clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE.** **Definition:** a translated node whose emphasis/link markup is authored ONLY in the HTML fallback, so `applyStaticI18n` destroys it on every load — in English too, which is why it survived ~140 sessions unnoticed. **Two shapes, and they need OPPOSITE fixes.** (a) `data-i18n-html`: the CSV value replaces `innerHTML`, so the fix is to move the markup INTO both cells (the site is already correct). (b) plain `data-i18n`: `js/i18n.js` does `el.textContent = t(k)`, so tags are dropped unconditionally and **the CSV cannot rescue them** — a tag in the cell would render as literal text — so the fix is to change the SITE to `data-i18n-html`. NO** (cosmetic in most carriers) **but do not retire on streak alone** — two of the six `-html` carriers were `<a href>`, i.e. a dead empty-state link and a dead attribution credit, and one plain carrier dropped the Hebrew-font `<span>` around vav-holam/shuruk. - **class-only-selected-state**: **re-swept 2026-08-26 (S258 Pass A, LIVE across 10 pages) - hits: 2 carriers, both fixed in-pass (`2bc3db3` torah `.tt-jump-chip`, `cb95115` FM `#helpTabs`), 1 more logged at the pattern cap (`#qaTabs`); clean streak: 0 - ACTIVE.** **The detection definition is now settled after four shapes in one pass, and three of the four were killed by their own control arm.** The signature that works is **`classList.toggle('<mark>', <expr> === <shared current value>)`** - a two-arg toggle whose condition is an EQUALITY TEST against one shared value is the mutually-exclusive-selector idiom, and it self-controls (27 suite sites DO write aria on that path, so a zero is provably real). Rejected shapes, recorded so they are not re-tried: a guessed marker-class keyword list is BLIND (its control would not fire); "exactly one sibling carries an extra class" fires but is 20/20 false positives (it cannot separate a STATE class from a VARIANT class - `.btn-primary`, `.danger`, `.gold`, `.pulse-attn`); a bare group-toggle grep conflates selection with `collapsed`/`dragging`/`flipped`/`shuffling`. **And the source result is only a candidate list: re-check LIVE.** Source flagged 86 sites and rendered DOM cleared 85, because the aria is written centrally and far from the toggle (`initPillAria`'s MutationObserver covers 49 flash-card pills; the generator's `PILL_SEL`; the FM's `_syncTablist`). Count only INTERACTIVE elements when reading a ratio - the FM `[data-cat]` "7/20" was 13 non-interactive `.cat-panel` content divs. **Fix shape both carriers shared: the file already had the convention** (torah's own `setKaraokeActive` uses `aria-current`; the FM's `.wtab`/`.ctab` use `role=tab` + `_syncTablist`), so both fixes are convergence, and neither needed a CSV key.

- **debounced-persistence-with-no-page-hide-flush**: **re-swept 2026-08-26 (S258 Pass A) - hits: 1 NEW carrier (`classroom_dashboard.html`), fixed in-pass (`cf244df`); clean streak: 0 - ACTIVE, consequence-critical (data loss), never retires on streak.** **The hit widens the pattern: a "close-only" persistence is the same defect as a stranded timer.** The dashboard defers nothing on a timer, so a timer-shaped detector reports it clean - yet its settings reach storage only via `closeSettings()`, and leaving with the drawer open strands everything the 14 explicitly-saving controls do not cover. **Detection, generalised: find every write path into the persisted store, then ask what happens if the page is discarded before the one event that triggers it.** Measured consequence, not theorised: Restore-default reverted on screen while storage kept the old value, and a custom vowel colour never reached storage at all. **The fix's control arm is mandatory and specific here** - assert that the `visibilityState === 'visible'` branch does NOT write, or a naive save-on-every-visibility-change passes the loss probe identically. **Census filed as a standing measurement: all 8 tools are now covered** - 6 flush on the way out, and flash_cards/index provably need no flush (they write synchronously).

- **sub-floor touch target**: **re-swept 2026-08-26 (S258) - hits: 3 controls fixed (`bc6245d`, the FM guides/grid inputs), 1 refused with cause; clean streak: 0 - ACTIVE.** **New sub-shape worth keeping: a control whose size comes from a LAYOUT VARIABLE cannot take a `min-height`.** `#rulerCorner.rl-corner` is 22x22 because both dimensions are `var(--rl-w)`, the ruler thickness - it is the ruler system's corner cell, so raising it desyncs the rulers and raising the variable retunes the whole surface (a gate-3 geometry change). Distinguish these from the padding-sized shapes before proposing a one-line fix: `min-height` is right for a bespoke input rendering at its UA default (21px number fields, 16px range sliders), wrong for a cell in a coordinate system.

- **class-only-selected-state**: **re-swept 2026-08-26 (S257 Pass C, `Hebrew_Font_Maker.html`) - hits: 1 NEW carrier, fixed in-pass (`058d003`); clean streak: 0 - ACTIVE.** The carrier is the glyph-tile grid: `role="button"` tiles whose selected state was `.sel` (a navy plate) and nothing else - 209 tiles across 5 grids measured **0** with any selected-state ARIA, the selected one announcing the same shape as its 26 siblings. **Why S224's suite-wide run missed it, and the detector lesson:** the tiles are built by a JS decorator (`_a11yDecorateTile`) rather than authored in markup, and they are the suite's ONLY selection grid that is a `role="button"` div with no native input inside - a static markup scan sees nothing, and a live scan that groups by same-tag siblings still needs the control-not-region discipline the S226 refutation added. **Receipt, checked not assumed:** the generator's and flash cards' `.letter-tile` grids measure **31/31 with ARIA** and `.vowel-chip` wraps a native checkbox, so the class is clean outside this file.

- **row-siblings-with-mismatched-heights**: **re-swept 2026-08-26 (S257, the shared language switcher across 10 pages x EN/HE) - hits: 1 (one cause, 13 pages), fixed `980fbbb`; clean streak: 0 - ACTIVE.** The last known cause of an uneven header row, and the detector question it settles is **which value**, not whether: a fixed height cannot serve 13 different rows, and the measurement showed the candidate's own proposal (a fixed 35px) is **worse than doing nothing** (spread 98.0 vs 47.0). - **state-mutation-that-never-arms-its-persistence**: **re-swept 2026-08-26 (S257) - hits: 1, the knowingly-deferred `setInputMode`, now fixed (`57abf9c`); clean streak: 0 - ACTIVE (consequence-critical: data loss, so it never retires on streak).** **The fix shape is the finding worth keeping: when ONE caller is a boot-time restore, fix the SETTER and let that caller state its exception** - the inverse (teaching the setter to detect booting) leaves every future caller depending on a flag it cannot see. Use the file's existing clean-marker (`markClean()`) rather than a hand-rolled reset, because the snapshot must survive for the restore prompt. **The mandatory control arm must be BEHAVIOURAL, not a flag read:** wait past the full debounce and confirm nothing was written - a stale-but-cleared timer id makes the naive `timer === 0` assertion fail on correct code (see the S257 refutation candidate). **Still swept in only ONE file** - the dashboard, torah and trope settings blobs remain the place a second carrier would live.

- **state-mutation-that-never-arms-its-persistence**: **registered + first swept 2026-08-26 (S256 Pass B) - hits: 13 setters in `Hebrew_Font_Maker.html`, all fixed (`494aa68`); 1 knowingly deferred (`setInputMode`, needs a boot guard - filed P3). clean streak: 0 - ACTIVE, and consequence-critical (data loss), so it stays ACTIVE regardless of streak.** **Definition:** a setter writes into the app's PERSISTED state object and re-renders, but never calls that app's dirty/save scheduler - so the change is real on screen, correct in memory, and gone on reload. Distinct from `debounced-persistence-with-no-page-hide-flush`: there a timer is armed and never flushed; here **nothing is ever armed**, which also silences any unsaved-work guard reading the same flag and makes an explicit flush a no-op. **Detection:** parse the file into top-level function bodies; keep those that ASSIGN into the persisted root (`project.` / `settings.`); flag any whose body lacks a call to the scheduler (`markDirty()`) or to an undo helper that calls it. Exclude the engine's own restore/undo paths, lazy initialisers, render helpers and save routines (they legitimately do not dirty). **The control is mandatory and is what makes the result trustworthy: a fresh boot must read NOT dirty.** A naive fix that dirties at load looks identical on the persistence probe and is a regression. **Placement rule:** the scheduler call goes immediately after the assignment, not at the end of the body - a setter with an early return after assigning would otherwise skip it on exactly the interesting path. **Probe note:** an inline-script `let project` is NOT on `window`, so `window.project` reads undefined and a persistence probe silently reports every value as false.

- **flex-column-crushing-its-own-rows** (**NEW, registered 2026-08-23 (S249 Pass N arm 4)**): a `display:flex; flex-direction:column` container that is ALSO height-constrained and scrollable (`max-height`/`flex:1` + `overflow-y:auto`) silently **compresses its children instead of scrolling**, because every flex item defaults to `flex-shrink:1`. The compression is not shared evenly — it lands almost entirely on whichever child has the lowest min-content floor, and if that child carries `overflow:hidden` its contents are **clipped away and become un-hittable while still reporting a sane `getComputedStyle`**. Detection: for each element whose parent is a column flex container and whose own `flex-shrink !== 0`, compare `scrollHeight` to the rendered box height; flag when the gap exceeds ~3px, and treat `overflow:hidden` on the victim as the escalation to un-operable. **Invisible to a resized desktop window** — it only fires on a viewport short enough to overflow — so it needs real device descriptors or a deliberately short window. **hits this sweep: 1 consequential (`index.html` `.ie-modal-body` → `.ivrit-mode-toggle`, 33px→2px, Automatic/Manual unreachable by finger), fixed `2453788`; clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE.** **Suite-wide sweep run the same session over 10 pages × iPhone SE + iPhone 13** (index, generator, dashboard, flash cards, dictionary, torah, trope, Font Maker, resources, contact): after the fix **index reports 0 clipped**, and the only other `clipped` hit anywhere is `classroom_dashboard.html`'s `span#a11yStatus`, which is **correct by design** — the textbook visually-hidden live region (`width:1px;height:1px;clip-path:inset(50%)`) — and was verified as such rather than filed. flash_cards showed 31 crushed-but-unclipped items and a dedicated collision probe found **0 actual overlaps**, so those are benign wrappers. Generator, dictionary, resources and contact: 0 crushed. **Next sweep should re-run the same detector after any new modal/drawer with a scrolling flex column.**

- **legibility-destroyed-by-a-second-dimming-layer** (**NEW, registered 2026-08-23 (S248 Pass M)**): an element that is ALREADY quieted once — by a muted colour token, or by a translucent plate — is given a **group `opacity`** on top. The group opacity is the trap: it composites the element toward **whatever is behind it on the page**, not toward its own plate, so on a light surface it drags white text *lighter than the background it sits on* and muted text paler still. **The defect is invisible to a naive colour-pair check**, because `getComputedStyle(el).color` reports a perfectly good value — it only surfaces once cumulative ancestor `opacity` is composited into the foreground (exactly the probe correction S247 registered). Both of S248's contrast hits are this one shape in different clothes: `#fsExitBtn` (`opacity: 0.45` over an `rgba(13,18,32,0.55)` plate → **2.11:1** measured from pixels) and `.weather-attr` (`opacity: 0.85` over `var(--muted)` at 0.6rem → **4.35 / 4.04**). **The fix is always the same: delete the redundant layer, keep the intended one** — the plate carries the restraint, or the token does; never both. **Detection:** run the opacity-compositing contrast probe (never the naive one), then grep `opacity: 0\.` on any rule that also sets `color` or `background`. **Hits: 2, both fixed (`d31788c`, `57f379f`); clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE (consequence-critical: it is a readability class, and it re-enters any time a designer reaches for `opacity` to make something quiet).**

- **translated-sibling stray** (a display site rendering a raw English name/string while an authored AND translated key for that exact string is already used by a sibling site in the same file — often one or two lines away): **REGISTERED 2026-08-22 (S243) on its FOURTH occurrence**, exactly as the S218 entry instructed ("register it as a pattern if a fourth appears"). Lineage: S177 (2 FM button labels whose sibling `title=` was localized), S211, S218 (dictionary POS badges + FM composed-form tiles), **S243 (the QA grid rendering `esc(row.name)` where every other grid uses `gName()`, plus 3 stage strings whose keys were authored and translated and simply never wired)**. hits this sweep: **4 (all fixed in-pass — f50cd23, 81f8727)**, clean streak: 0 — **ACTIVE**. **Detection:** reverse-lookup the English visible in the Hebrew UI against `en.json`, keeping only keys whose `he.json` value DIFFERS (an untranslated key showing English is not this pattern); then confirm a *sibling* call site in the same file already uses that key or its helper. **False-positive classes already grounded, do not re-chase:** `<kbd>` key legends (Ctrl/Shift/Enter — printed on the physical key), font-family names ("Alef" ×6), preset name "Default", paper size "Letter", brand "TaL AM", the ~30 never-translate trope pronunciation names, and any literal sitting inside an `I18n.t`/`_pT`/`_drawT` fallback argument.

  _(prior)_ **re-swept 2026-08-25 (S255, SUITE-WIDE and MULTILINE-AWARE for the first time) — hits: 4 fixed across 3 files (`a014124` torah `#ttCopyRange`; `79565bf` contact `#cfName` + resources `#sgName`/`#sgResName`), 14 more logged as a P3 (Font Maker, never swept); clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE. 6th and 7th tools of the class, and the S245 backlog is now CLEAR.** **⚑ THE DETECTOR WAS BROKEN AND IS NOW FIXED: every prior sweep was LINE-BASED and silently skipped multi-line `<input>` tags** — which is why `#ttCopyRange` survived S245→S254 despite being named in three pointers. Multiline-aware (`re.S`) the suite has **56** typeable fields, 42 with no hint of any kind (per-file breakdown in the standing-measurement candidate). **"No hint" is NOT "defect":** prose fields must KEEP the sentence default, and `type=email`/`type=url` are already handled by the platform — S255 left 7 such fields untouched deliberately and asserted them as a control arm in every verification cell. _(prior: **re-swept 2026-08-25 (S254, `classroom_dashboard`) — hits: 5, ALL fixed `118f979`. 4th tool of the class, S247 backlog cleared.**)_ The five fields S247 logged-not-fixed (`#pickerRoster`, `#presetName`, `#swmSaveName`, `#locationInput`, `#frLocationInput`) all took `autocapitalize="words" autocorrect="off" spellcheck="false"`. **⚑ REFINED DETECTION RULE, and it changes what a "fix" looks like: this class has THREE right answers, not one.** A URL/code field wants `autocapitalize="off"` (the S244/S239 shape); a **name or place** field wants `"words"` — capitalising each word is the desired behaviour and only autocorrect/spellcheck are hostile; a numeric field wants `inputmode`/`type="number"` and nothing else (`#timerCustomInput` and `#groupN` were already correct and are NOT hits). **Sweeping for "missing `autocapitalize`" and stamping `off` everywhere would have made the roster and the city fields worse.** Remaining known carriers, both logged and unfixed at the 2/tool cap: `torah_trainer#ttCopyRange` (S245) and `flash_cards#shareCodeOutput` (S244, unverifiable headless).

Logged as a Candidate, NOT fixed: the dashboard was at the 2/tool cap. **Standing lesson: fixing one field on a page does not clear the page** — sweep every text-bearing input on a carrier, not the one the arm happened to surface.
