The page's three `type="number"` fields were held as the control. clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE.**

- **i18n cross-column parity (placeholders, plurals, inline markup)**: **REGISTERED 2026-08-19 (S230) — a NEW pattern, owned by pass K. hits this sweep: 1 real (`dictionary.translit.credit`, fixed 63b15bf) + 1 logged-by-design (`shared.folders.empty_list`, closed 3fc6bda by gate 2). clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE.** **Detection (two detectors, both cheap, both must be run against a control first):** parse `locales/ui-strings.csv` and compare each language column against `en` for (1) identical `{placeholder}` sets, (2) `.one`/`.other` pairing, (3) leading/trailing non-letter affixes, (4) identical-to-English cells, (5) an `he` cell with no Hebrew letters, and (6) **identical inline-HTML tag sets and `<a href>` counts**. **Detector (6) is the one that earns its keep** — a key consumed via `data-i18n-html` whose markup exists in one column and not another silently destroys a link or emphasis in the other language, and nothing else in the toolchain sees it. **Known false-positive classes, all verified in S230 and NOT to be re-chased:** `.one` plurals idiomatically dropping `{count}` (“מילה אחת” *is* “one word”); `.other` as a real key name (part-of-speech “Other”) and `.one` as a mode name (“1-Letter”); identical cells that are licence ids, brand names, bare numerals, pure `{a} ({b})` format strings or symbols; and affix deltas that are Hebrew typography (geresh ׳, gershayim ״, maqaf ־, sof pasuk ׃) or an RTL arrow flip (`.dir-arrow` mirrors those in CSS, so the CSV keeps the LTR glyph). **Normalise those before reading a count: raw 236 → 1.**

- **horizontal-overflow-at-narrow-widths**: **re-swept 2026-08-29 (S290 Pass N, `Hebrew_Font_Maker.html`) — hits: 0 across 15 cells; clean streak: +1 — ACTIVE.** **⚑⚑ THE DETECTOR THIS PATTERN AND PASS N's ARM 1 HAD BEEN USING CANNOT FIRE ON A PHONE — read this before any future narrow-width sweep.** `documentElement.scrollWidth > window.innerWidth` is what the skill's arm-1 recipe specifies, and on a REAL device descriptor it is structurally blind: the mobile layout viewport INFLATES to swallow the overflow, so both sides move together (control: injecting a 900px element moved `scrollWidth` AND `innerWidth` 390→900, and the comparison still read `false`). `documentElement.clientWidth`, `visualViewport.width`, `body.clientWidth` and `outerWidth` all stay pinned at the device width and DO discriminate — **use `clientWidth`**. S290 re-measured all 15 cells with the working detector, so its clean is earned; **every earlier N that used `innerWidth` has an unearned arm 1** and should not be cited as evidence. _(prior: **⚑ S247 confirms the CLIPPED-not-scrolled variant S245 registered, and sharpens it into a detection rule: measure each control's visible fraction against its nearest `overflow:hidden` ancestor, and HIT-TEST it.** On the dashboard at 320px the "Long" date format measured **0% visible with `elementFromPoint` returning null** while `document.scrollWidth` sat at exactly 320 — the registered `docW <= innW` detector cannot see this class at all, by construction. The clipper here is `.panel { overflow: hidden }`, which exists to clip the panel title to its rounded corners, so the shape recurs anywhere a non-wrapping flex row sits inside a rounded panel. **Two probe traps found while measuring it, both of which fabricated overflow that was not there:** a rect read BEFORE `scrollIntoView` reported a phantom 67.3px overflow, and a **zero-width collapsed element** reports a rect at (0,0), which reads as a full-width overflow — filter `width < 1` before believing any overflow number. _(prior)_ **⚑ S245 (Pass N, torah_trainer) adds a FIFTH cause the existing detector is blind to by construction: CLIPPED, not scrolled.** The per-verse action row laid out 18px (EN) / 30px (HE) wider than a 320px viewport, yet `scrollWidth` stayed exactly 320 — because `.tt-verse` clips its overflow, so the page never widens and the button is simply cut in half (Copy rendered as a bare "C" on every verse). **Every arm of this pattern to date asserts `scrollWidth - clientWidth === 0`, which is TRUE in this failure.** Add the second assertion: census every visible element for `rect.right > clientWidth` or `rect.left < 0`. Fixed `0da7574`. Prior: **re-swept 2026-08-20 (S232, closing the S213 P3 that had outlived the S230 receipt): 26/26 arms 0px + 0 pageerrors at 320px over the post-S231-footer + S232-feature surface — clean streak: 2 — ACTIVE** (consequence-critical, never auto-retires). Prior: **swept 2026-08-19 (S230) — CLEAN SUITE-WIDE FOR THE FIRST TIME: 13 pages × en/he = 26 arms, every one 0px at 320px, 0 pageerrors. hits this session: 1 page (the Font Maker, the last carrier), fixed across `6eb47bb` + `e01ce03`. clean streak: 1 — ACTIVE** (consequence-critical: a WCAG 1.4.10 AA failure, and new CSS reintroduces it cheaply). **S230 added a fourth cause and a method note: (d) a flex ITEM that refuses to shrink (`flex:0 0 auto`) floors its parent no matter how much `min-width:0` you put on ancestors, and (e) `flex-direction:column` + `align-items:flex-start` makes every child size to its own content, so a container’s `flex:1`/`min-width:0` silently stop applying on the cross axis. Attribute lever-by-lever — the Font Maker’s 413px read like one unwrapped row and was four separate causes, the largest worth only 72%.** **S231 adjacent work (not a sweep — streak untouched): the four remaining hard 1fr-footer grids converged on the proven auto-fit form preventively (5c5422d, 24/24 wide arms pixel-identical), and the S227 sub-element INTERNAL-overflow backlog closed (eb8f078; resources measured already-clean) — the reflow thread now has zero open items at any level, page or sub-element.** Prior: **REGISTERED 2026-08-19 (S228) — the shape six sessions had been fixing one instance at a time without a health line. hits this session: 2, both fixed (`b3c4f52` torah_trainer, `a2aaa88` contact). clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE.** **Detection:** load each of the 13 pages at a 320px viewport over local HTTP, dismiss auto-open overlays, and read `document.documentElement.scrollWidth - window.innerWidth`; **run EN and HE separately — the two directions find DIFFERENT defects** (contact's honeypot was 9999px in HE and 0 in EN; torah's Layout control was 11px in EN and 0 in HE, because the English labels are wider). **Two causes seen so far:** (a) a flex row with no `flex-wrap` whose children are `flex:none` (the chrome-page headers, the three tool header rows, torah's `.radio-group`); (b) an element parked off-screen with a PHYSICAL offset (`left:-9999px`), which is inert in one direction and scrollable overflow in the other. **A logical property does not fix (b)** — it mirrors the bug rather than removing it; clip in place instead. **Verification rule:** measure with the fix stashed AND applied using the same probe, and assert inertness above the breakpoint (identical geometry with the rule forced off vs on) — a wrap rule that changes desktop layout is a regression, not a fix. **State at registration: 12 of 13 pages clean in both directions; `Hebrew_Font_Maker.html` is the sole carrier left (413 EN / 269 HE at 320) and is an open P3 candidate.**)

- **hover-only-affordance-under-a-synthetic-mouse-event**: **re-swept 2026-08-23 (S249 Pass N arm 4) — hits: 1, the THIRD and FINAL carrier (`hebrew_dictionary.html`), fixed `383aa2a`; clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE.** **The class is now fully swept: all three `bindTip` carriers are fixed** (trope_tutor + torah_trainer in S248, dictionary here). **S248's open thread is closed with a receipt, not a guess** — the dictionary's five `.tip-wrap`s measured zero-width because they sit behind **TWO independent collapse layers**, the `.panel` AND the inner `.adv-section`, and **both rules are `display:none !important`**, so forcing an inline `display:block` on either ancestor does nothing; only removing the `.collapsed` class from both reveals them (20×15), after which one tap demonstrably leaves the tip closed on iPhone 13 and iPad. **Method note for the next sweep: the fix must be ADAPTED, not pasted** — the dictionary's `hide()` takes no argument where the torah/trope twins take `hide(wrap)`; the three implementations are siblings, not a `═══` byte-identical block. **And prove desktop is unchanged by MEASURING the pre-fix file** (`git stash` → re-run → restore), not by reasoning: a synthetic mouse click fires `pointerenter` before `click`, so the first desktop click closes a hover-opened tip both before and after the fix.
  _(prior)_ **hover-only-affordance-under-a-synthetic-mouse-event**: **swept 2026-08-23 (S248 Pass N arm 4), first sweep since registration — hits: 2 MORE carriers (`trope_tutor.html`, `torah_trainer.html`), both fixed in one commit `2168a8f`; a 3rd (`hebrew_dictionary.html`) carries the shape but could not be surfaced headless and was logged, not changed; clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE.** The sweep confirmed the pattern's own S247 warning that it STACKS and that source-reading cannot find it: on all three pages the layer-1 `pointerType === 'mouse'` hover guard was already correct, and only the **`focus`** layer was open — `bindTip` puts `tabindex="0"` on the `.tip-wrap`, so a pointer press focuses it before its own click lands (`focus → show`, `click → isShown() → hide`). Traced with a live event log under a device descriptor, with the **S247-fixed dashboard as a must-pass control** that stayed green. **Detection, sharpened:** grep is only a shortlist (`addEventListener('focus'` / `mouseenter` on any tap target) — the verdict must be a real `page.touchscreen.tap()` under `devices[...]` that checks the bubble is still open 400 ms later.
  _(prior)_ **hover-only-affordance-under-a-synthetic-mouse-event** (**NEW, registered 2026-08-23 (S247 Pass N arm 4)**): a control whose reveal is wired to raw `mouseenter`/`mouseleave` (or to an unguarded `focus`) **plus** a `click` that TOGGLES the same state. On a touch device the tap fires a synthetic `mouseenter` — and a press focuses a `tabindex`-bearing target — *before* the click lands, so the click sees the state already open and closes it: the affordance opens and shuts within one gesture and is **unreachable on a phone**, where `(hover:none)` is true and there is no other way in. **hits: 1 (`classroom_dashboard.html`, all 3 drawer tooltips), fixed `3c842ae`; clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE.** **Detection:** trace the real event sequence under a device descriptor (`page.tap`, capture-phase listeners logging the target's computed display) — do NOT read the source and reason, because the defect is an ORDERING between two handlers that both look correct in isolation, and it stacks in layers (S247 fixed the hover layer and the identical focus-layer race appeared underneath it). **Fix vehicle:** gate hover on `e.pointerType === 'mouse'` (the form `hebrew_dictionary.html`'s `bindTip` already uses) and gate `focus` behind a pointerdown flag so keyboard focus still reveals. **Exemption:** a control that ALSO has a non-hover path to the same information is a paper-cut, not a hit. **Unswept elsewhere** — the other `.tip-wrap`/`bindTip`/`tooltip-wrap` carriers (dictionary, torah_trainer, trope_tutor, flash_cards, generator) have NOT been touch-traced; the dictionary's *code* is the correct form but its touch behaviour was never empirically confirmed (S247's attempt to do so was invalid — that page has no `#tipFloat`).

- **contrast-inverted-by-a-hover-or-active-state** (**NEW, registered 2026-08-23 (S247 Pass M)**): a `:hover`/`:active` rule that changes BOTH the background and the text colour, landing on a pair with LESS contrast than the rest state. **hits: 1 (`hebrew_blend_generator.html` `.btn-primary:hover`, 3.36:1 against a 5.43:1 rest state), fixed `3421074`; clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE (consequence-critical: it is a readability failure, so it carries pass C's severity).** **Detection:** measure contrast in the hover state as well as at rest, in BOTH themes, and **from rendered pixels** where a `filter` is involved. **The theme asymmetry is the trap:** `var(--white)` is `#1e2535` in dark, so a flip-to-white hover FAILS in light and accidentally PASSES in dark — the inverse of the usual dark-mode assumption, and the reason this survived. **Fix vehicle:** the suite's dominant gold-button hover idiom is `filter: brightness(1.06)` (7 carriers), which changes no colour pair and therefore cannot invert contrast.

- **row-siblings-with-mismatched-heights**: **re-swept 2026-08-23 (S246 Pass M) under a TWICE-corrected detector — hits: 4 pages (one cause), all fixed `91c57ab`; clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE.** `.hbtn` measured 27px against two 30px siblings on resources / contact / privacy / terms. **The detector needed a second correction and this is the important part:** S245's prescribed fix (group strictly by the parent element) over-corrects on a wrapping grid — index.html's 8-card `.cards` reported a 43px "spread" that is only row 1 being shorter than row 3. v3 groups by parent, then clusters children whose vertical extents **overlap** (centre-aligned siblings always overlap = one row; grid rows never do = separate rows). Validated both directions on index.html. Residual known false positive: structurally heterogeneous flex children (a star + a heading block + a control group is not a control row) — logged as a candidate. **Standing lesson, now demonstrated twice in two sessions: a corrected detector inherits the blind spots of whatever corrected it — re-run the census both directions before trusting either verdict.**
  _(prior)_ **⚑ RE-OPENED 2026-08-23 (S245 Pass M) — the S226 "class CLOSED, 0 groups on all 10 pages" claim was built on a detector with a FALSE-NEGATIVE mode, and at least one carrier survived it.** `trope_tutor.html` ran a **5px** spread across its six `.hright` controls (Home 34.38 / switcher 30 / Tour 31 / fullscreen 30 / dark 35 / gear 35) — and the S225 sweep-status line lists that very page under "Clean". **Mechanism, reproduced with the fix suppressed:** grouping by `parent.className + round(rect.top/6)` splits ONE row whenever `align-items:center` offsets its short controls into the next bucket — `hright|3` held Home/dark/gear (spread 0.62px) and `hright|4` held Tour/fullscreen (spread 1.0px), both comfortably under the 1.2px threshold, so a ragged row reported as two tidy ones. **S226 had already written this failure mode down** ("the `round(top/6)` grouping drops a control that is already the outlier") but applied it only while *grounding a hit* on the dashboard; the census itself was never re-run under the corrected rule. **CORRECTED DETECTION (use this, not the S225 definition): group by the parent row ELEMENT — never by a rounded top coordinate — and census EVERY child of that row.** Fixed on the found carrier (`57d5e68`, `min-height:35px`, the `db37a54` declaration). **Suite re-census under the corrected detector, 10 pages × EN/HE at 1280 (S245): 7 pages still show a spread, but on 5 of them the sole remaining cause is the shared 30px `.i18n-select` language switcher** — which is NOT a defect (S196 deliberately raised it to the 30px floor) but a convergence decision logged as its own candidate. Genuinely clean under the corrected rule: generator, Font Maker, index. hits this sweep: 1 (fixed), clean streak: 0 — **ACTIVE**. Prior: **swept 2026-08-19 (S226 Pass A, 2nd sweep) — hits: the 3 known carriers, ALL fixed in-pass (`db37a54`); the class is now CLOSED: 0 groups on all 10 pages, with the 7 already-clean pages held as a CONTROL. clean streak: 0 (this sweep found and fixed, it did not come back empty) — ACTIVE.** Registered + first swept 2026-08-19 (S225 Pass M): 5 of 10 pages hit, 2 fixed then (`b55b7d5` Font Maker toolbar, `13de328` dictionary toolbar) at the 2/session cap. **Detection definition (unchanged, and it re-found exactly the 3 known carriers, so it is calibrated):** for every visible control (`button,select,input,a.hbtn,.tbtn,.mode-btn,.ctl-btn,.wtab,.ctab`) whose parent computes to a **row** flex container (`display:*flex*`, `flex-direction` not `column*`), group by `parent.className + round(rect.top/6)` and flag any group of ≥2 whose `max(height) − min(height) > 1.2px`. **Exclusions:** `type=range|checkbox|radio|color|file`, column parents, non-flex parents. **Two refinements from S226.** (1) The `round(top/6)` grouping **drops a control that is already the outlier** — the dashboard's 41px `#fsBtn` sat in its own single-member group and was never reported; the row's true spread was 10px, not the 4px the detector printed. When grounding a hit, census EVERY child of the row, not the detector's groups. (2) A row's decorative children (the generator's `✡︎` star span, title/switcher DIVs) are not controls and must be excluded from any pass/fail assertion, or a correct fix reads as a failure. **Causes seen, in frequency order:** a variant declaring `border:none` where siblings carry one (S225 ×2); **font-size alone deciding the line box** — 1rem icon buttons beside 0.82rem text buttons, with no shared height declared (S226 ×3, every carrier); and a **compound-selector specificity bug** silently discarding a variant's own padding (S226 ×1). **Convergence target is the row's own tallest control and never below the ratified 30px floor (S102)** — converging up shrinks no glyph. **Reference implementations: Font Maker `.hbtn` and Flash Cards `.h-btn`, clean because every header control goes through ONE class.**

- **debounced-persistence-with-no-page-hide-flush**: **swept 2026-08-19 (S226 Pass A, 2nd sweep) — hits: 1 NEW carrier (`hebrew_dictionary.html`), fixed in-pass (`18c54ff`); the 3 known carriers re-checked and holding. clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE, and consequence-critical (data loss), so it stays ACTIVE regardless of streak.** Registered + first swept 2026-08-16 (S223 Pass B): 2 of 3 carriers hit, both fixed (`aeb7809`). **Definition:** a store written through a **debounced** timer (`clearTimeout(x); x = setTimeout(() => localStorage.setItem(…), N)`) with **no flush on page hide**, so a page discarded inside the window never runs the pending callback and the write is lost silently. **Detection (the control is mandatory):** a **pick → leave-immediately → re-read** probe run twice per carrier — dwell 0, and a dwell longer than the debounce as the CONTROL; a same-tick re-read passes on a broken carrier because the in-memory object is already correct. **Census method — SHARPENED in S226, and this is what found the new carrier:** run TWO greps and compare them as a table — a debounce-timer signature (`_*T(imer) = setTimeout` / `clearTimeout(_*save|persist)`) against a `addEventListener('pagehide'|'visibilitychange')` signature. At S226 that read FM 5/2, torah 5/2, trope 3/2, dashboard 0/2, **dictionary 1/0** — the single row where the two disagree is the hit, and it takes seconds. **S223's per-tool verdicts are NOT a safe baseline:** it cleared the dictionary on 12/12 scalar-pref round trips at dwell 0, and those prefs genuinely are synchronous — but `hebrewDictionary_lastState` is a separate writer with its own 1000 ms debounce, and probing a tool's other keys never reaches it. **Probe the key each writer owns, not the tool.** **Carriers:** `torah_trainer`, `trope_tutor`, `hebrew_dictionary` (all HIT, all fixed), `Hebrew_Font_Maker` (**the reference implementation**: `visibilitychange`(hidden) + `pagehide` → `flushAutosave()`). generator, flash cards and dashboard remain synchronous-write, verified rather than assumed. **Fix shape:** adopt the Font Maker's listener pair verbatim; `unload`/`beforeunload` are unreliable on mobile and must not be substituted. If the page's save carries a guard (torah's `_handoutActive`), the flush must carry it too.

- **async-store-backed-choice-clobbered-by-a-sync-fallback**: **swept 2026-08-19 (S226 Pass A, 2nd sweep) — CLEAN with receipts, extended past fonts as its own note directed. clean streak: 1 — ACTIVE, and consequence-critical (it destroys saved user data), so it does NOT retire on a 3-clean streak.** Registered + first swept 2026-08-16 (S222 Pass F): 3 of 6 carriers hit, all fixed (`c16c558`, `f424ea6`). **Definition:** a setting whose valid values arrive from an ASYNC store is read back by a SYNC resolver that falls back to a default for an unrecognised name — **and then writes that default back into the persisted settings**. The write-back is the defect, not the fallback. **Detection (do not weaken it):** (1) grep every `find(…) || <default>` / `? name : <default>` in a settings-restore path, then check whether the resolved value is ASSIGNED to persisted state; (2) never trust a same-tick check — pick, reload, re-read; (3) **test a store-backed value, never a built-in**; (4) check the guard AND the caller. **S226 adds rule (5), learned the hard way: a GHOST name is not a store-backed value.** An arm that seeds a name with no IndexedDB record reported **2 CLOBBERED of 5**, one of them on a page this line names as the reference implementation. The decisive arm — write a real font into `ivritsuite-fonts`, pick it through the page's own `setHebFont`, reload — **PASSES on torah, trope and dashboard**: the record resolves before any write. torah/trope normalise an unknown name to the default and dashboard/dictionary/generator leave it in place; both behaviours are safe. **Coverage beyond fonts (S226, the first time this was done):** the only two `|| <default>` resolvers outside the font pickers are read-path (dashboard `applyFontChoice`'s editor `face=` string — logged separately as a *content* consequence, not this pattern; torah's `renderText` font stack, which bails to `'serif'`), and torah's five parsha-restore sites all **bail** rather than write back. **Reference implementations:** `hebrew_dictionary.html` / `trope_tutor.html`. **Where else to look next:** any picker whose options come from IndexedDB or a `fetch` — fonts and the parsha picker are now both covered.

- **rebuild-where-a-class-swap-would-do**: **REGISTERED 2026-08-16 (S220)** — not yet swept suite-wide, hits: 1 (`26b9e7e`), clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE. **Definition:** a settings toggle whose visual effect is ALREADY gated in CSS on a body/root class, yet whose handler calls the page's full re-render instead of the cheap class+var swap. **Detection:** for each `settings.<flag>` written by a change handler, grep whether the flag's rendered effect is reachable through a `body.<class>` selector (or a CSS custom property) that some `apply*Colors()`-style chokepoint already toggles; if it is, a `renderText()`/`render*()` call in that handler is a hit. **Two known instances, both on `torah_trainer.html`** — the S60 nikkud layer (fixed long ago) and `colorCodeTrope` (S220). **No other tool has been checked**, and the shape is generic: any tool with a CSS-var colour layer and a master toggle can carry it. **Watch for the split that makes it safe:** an export/copy path that reads the classes off detached markup must keep its own gating, or removing the guard changes what the user pastes or prints (see `26b9e7e`'s `_inlineCopyStyles` carve-out).

This is NOT a sweep of the class and does not advance its streak; it is a receipt that the class's remaining known surface is currently clean, recorded so the next A does not re-derive it.)_

- **decorative-glyph-carrier-exposed-to-assistive-tech** (**2nd instance fixed 2026-08-15, S219, c2399f1 — Font Maker QA column heads**. That instance sharpened the pattern in a way every future sweep needs: **`aria-label` on the element is NOT a fix for this class.** The FM header already had `aria-label`, so the `<th>`'s NAME was correct and a name-level check passed — but the carrier span and its text node remain in the accessibility tree beneath it (**34 dotted-circle names across 51 nodes**, → 0 across 17 after marking the span `aria-hidden`). So detection must look at the SUBTREE, not the accessible name, and must use `page.accessibility.snapshot({interestingOnly:false})` — the default prunes exactly these nodes and returns an empty set that reads as a clean pass. Second half of the S213 candidate (`templateCellHTML`) closed as NOT-APPLICABLE: it feeds `renderTemplateCanvases`, so its carrier is ink on a printed sheet, not an AT node — **a carrier inside a canvas-rasterised surface is out of scope for this pattern**.) Original definition: a glyph rendered on a **placeholder carrier character** — U+25CC DOTTED CIRCLE for an isolated combining mark — where the carrier is the only pronounceable part of the node, so assistive tech announces "dotted circle" in place of a mark it cannot voice. A **hit** requires the glyph to be a DUPLICATE: the same item's name must already be on screen adjacent to it (or on the node itself, via `aria-label`/`title`). Where the glyph IS the content (an identify-the-mark question), leaving it exposed is correct and hiding it would destroy the task — so the detection is "carrier + a sibling name", never "carrier". Detection: grep the carrier codepoint suite-wide, then ground each site by reading its builder. Swept **2026-08-15 (S213)** over `trope_tutor.html` only: **4 carrier call sites → 2 hits (fixed f207a34), 1 already correct** (`c-glyph`, whose button carries `aria-label = tropeName`), **1 correct-as-exposed** (the drill question). **Surface NOT yet covered: `Hebrew_Font_Maker.html`'s 2 visual carriers** (logged as a candidate). hits: 2, clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE

Every pattern's streak and last-swept date is unchanged from S203's sweep; the trio of consequence-critical patterns stays ACTIVE regardless. **No new pattern registered:** the Pass F divergence is one shipped micro-feature that has not been replicated, which is F's own remit, not a recurring code shape.)_

- **error-status-clobbered-by-a-later-routine-write** (**NEW, registered S199**): a status/live-region line that correctly reports a FAILURE is then overwritten, on the same code path, by a later **routine** write that assumes the happy state — so the diagnostic exists in the source, fires, and is gone before the user reads it, leaving advice that the failure itself made impossible. Sibling of `wired-then-clobbered label` (S192), but the victim is an **error message** rather than a translated label, and the clobberer is a normal-path status write rather than a JS setter. **Detection: never by reading the code** — both call sites look correct in isolation. Force the failure (block the tool's `data/` corpus with `serviceWorkers:'block'`), then read the tool's OWN `[role=status]`/live-region element at the END of init and compare it against the message the catch set. **Do NOT regex body text for `fail|error|…`** — that produced a false negative here on both carriers (curly apostrophes, and wording like "unavailable"). Swept 2026-08-12 (S199 Pass B), hits: **1** (torah_trainer, fixed b5bd9c0), clean: trope_tutor + dictionary. **Re-swept 2026-08-15 (S212 Pass B) on S199's own instruction to widen to non-init failure paths — hits: 1** (flash_cards, fixed 80695d9). **⚑ SURFACE CORRECTED: it is 5 tools, not 3.** S199 scoped the class to "the 3 tools that fetch a `data/` corpus at load" and wrote off "the other 4" — but flash_cards and the generator fetch `data/hebrew_words.json` **lazily**, so they carry the class and sat outside the declared surface for 13 sessions. Flash cards was the hit; the generator is clean **because it already had the fix** (`_realWordsFailed`), which is where the flash-cards patch was copied from. Clobberer definition widened too: not only an end-of-init routine write but **any later routine re-render**, of which a language switch is the cheapest universal trigger (`applyI18n` re-renders every page's JS-built content). Clean this sweep: dictionary, torah_trainer, trope_tutor, generator. **Detection, both traps now recorded: do NOT regex body prose** — S199's regex produced a false NEGATIVE (curly apostrophes, "unavailable"), and S212's produced three false POSITIVES by being English-only across a language switch. Read the specific element, and make the re-render probe language-agnostic (switch EN→HE→EN, so a merely TRANSLATED message returns while a destroyed one stays gone). Clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE.

- **animation-outside-its-reduced-motion-block** (**NEW, registered S198**): a CSS `transition`/`animation` declaration whose selector is **not covered by its own page's `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block** — so a reader who asked the OS for less motion still gets that one. CLAUDE.md makes the coverage binding ("if you add an animation to a page, that page needs the reduced-motion block, and your animation must honor it"), which is exactly why a *partial* block is the dangerous shape: the block's presence reads as compliance. **Detection (cheap, mechanical, no rendering needed):** for each file, collect every selector carrying a `transition:`/`animation:` declaration outside the reduced-motion block, then subtract the selectors named inside it; anything left is a candidate. **Confirm at runtime with a control arm** — read `transitionDuration` under `reducedMotion:'reduce'` **and** `'no-preference'`; a probe that reports `0s` in both states is measuring nothing. **The sibling heuristic is what found S198's hit:** elements that *travel together* (a drawer and its backdrop, a modal and its scrim) must be neutralized together, and a block naming one but not the other is the tell. Swept 2026-08-12 (S198): **1 hit / 3 carriers of the settings drawer** — `torah_trainer` (fixed 915526d); `classroom_dashboard` and `trope_tutor` already correct. **Not yet swept suite-wide** — S198 censused only the `.settings-backdrop` shape; the full 11-page selector-subtraction sweep is the next A run's job. ACTIVE, clean streak 0. **⚑ FIRST GENERAL SWEEP 2026-08-12 (S199): 4 hits, all fixed (6fcf9e4).** Surface: all 12 pages, current-state. **Detection is now settled, and two thresholds must be right or the number is meaningless:** run the page under `reducedMotion:'reduce'` and read COMPUTED `transition-duration`/`animation-*` — but (a) **`0.00001s` is the neutralizer idiom (`0.01ms !important`) and counts as COVERAGE, not a hit**, so threshold at >1ms, and (b) bucket by transitioned **property**: explicit `transform`/position/size (and any keyframe animation) is the defect; a hover **colour/opacity** fade is not, and lumping them in inflates ~16 real hits to ~108. Result: keyframe animations already neutralized on **every** page (0 suite-wide); the escapees were 4 explicit `transform` transitions on 4 pages (`404 .home-btn`, `generator .vg-arrow`, `dashboard .day-item`, `dictionary #fsBtn`), each on a page whose block already existed and simply omitted them. **Fix-shape note: `!important` is usually REQUIRED, not stylistic** — a media query adds no specificity, so an equal-specificity rule declared later in the file wins (404's fix parsed fine and did nothing until it was added), and `.vg-arrow` carries its transition as an **inline** style. Clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE. **Remaining, deliberately NOT claimed as defects:** the `transition: all` hover declarations on generator/dashboard/dictionary/torah (see Candidates). **S204 detection refinement: the census MUST include bare-duration shorthands — `transition: 0.2s` is implicit `all` and a literal-'all' grep misses it (3 of torah's 8 real sites were this shape, one hiding the toggle-knob translateX, the class's first real motion hit). transition:all arm status after S204: dictionary S203 + generator/torah S204 CLOSED; dashboard is the last arm.** **S205: the transition:all backlog candidate is fully CLOSED (all four arms + flash_cards clean by census); the PATTERN stays ACTIVE for new code.**

- **content-dependent-tour-step-miscounts-the-tour** (**NEW, registered S197**): a guided-tour step whose `target()` only exists once remote/corpus content has rendered. The engines all skip an unresolvable step **silently by design** ("skip gracefully when hidden"), but the step counter is built from the **raw array index**, so on any failed/absent load the number **jumps and over-promises** — the teacher watches steps vanish. **Detection (cheap, ~2 min/tool): walk the real tour on a fresh profile and compare steps SHOWN against `TOUR_STEPS.length`; then re-walk with that tool's own corpus route-aborted.** The second arm is what makes it discriminating — the first arm alone only catches tools whose content is EXTERNAL (torah/Sefaria), and silently passes every tool served from local `data/`. **Fix shape: count by PRESENCE of each target, never visibility** — absent = content never arrived; hidden = a collapsed panel that opens fine. Presence is also the only side-effect-free probe: testing visibility means running every step's `reveal()`, which in the dictionary opens the sidebar and expands panels the tour hasn't reached. FIRST sweep 2026-08-12 (S197 Pass I), all 7 tour-bearing tools: **2 carriers found, both fixed → 0 remaining** (`torah_trainer.html`, `hebrew_dictionary.html`). **trope_tutor is the documented NEGATIVE — it has a content-dependent step too (`#tuCards .tu-card`) yet holds 6/6 with data blocked**, which is what proves the detector isn't just reporting "blocking data breaks tours". The other 4 tools target static chrome only. **Clean streak: 0 (first sweep, hits found).** ACTIVE.

- **per-sample-repaint-of-an-O(n)-live-preview** (**NEW, registered S196**): a continuous gesture — `pointermove`, a slider drag — that rebuilds an **O(n) preview from its whole accumulated buffer once per input SAMPLE** rather than once per animation frame, so the gesture is O(n²) in its own length. The screen cannot show more than one repaint per frame, so every extra rebuild is pure waste, and the cost is invisible at the short strokes/small drags a developer tests with. **Detection:** find the expensive builder call inside a `pointermove`/`oninput` handler where the builder walks a whole array; then, under **PACED** input (yield to rAF between batches — a synchronous dispatch loop starves rAF and fakes a 100× win), count builder invocations against frames. A per-sample handler shows `invocations == accepted samples`; a correct one shows `invocations ≈ frames`. Confirm with a first-10%-vs-last-10% mean ratio per sample — a flat ratio is clean, a rising one is the class. **Fix idiom (already in-tree twice):** `boldGenSet` and `nodeStatusCoords` — coalesce with an rAF token on the gesture object, re-read state at frame time (never snapshot), and guard the callback with `gesture !== g` so an ended gesture paints nothing. **Found + fixed 2026-08-12 (S196, Pass D): 1 hit** — Font Maker's four styled draw pens (2e09c29); its round pen is the same shape but measured under budget and deliberately left (logged as a Candidate with the two inputs that would make it actionable). **⚑ Notable: S85's Pass D fixed this exact shape in the same tool** (Generate Bold's per-frame warning scan), and Draw mode reintroduced it 111 sessions later — so this class recurs *within* a tool as new gesture surfaces are built. Clean streak: 0 (first sweep). Correctness-adjacent (degrades the primary drawing interaction), not consequence-critical.

- **false-positive-validator-on-the-app's-own-content** (**NEW, registered S194**): a QA/lint/warning rule whose **detector is broader than the failure it warns about**, so it fires on artwork or data the app itself ships — the user cannot act on it, cannot clear it, and it is present in **every** project, which is precisely how a panel of real warnings gets trained into background noise. Founding instance: the Font Maker outline scan flagging its own built-in **Comma** and **Semicolon** (`glyphOutlineScan` tested "do two contours' edges cross" while the message promised "can fill **inverted**" — inversion needs *opposite* winding, and both glyphs are all-outer, so nonzero simply unions them). **Detection:** for each validator, run it on a **pristine/empty project** — anything it reports there is by definition not the user's doing. Cheap (one page-evaluate) and it generalizes past contrast/i18n to every warning surface: FM QA, the export guard, the dictionary/flash-cards load states. **Second question once a hit is found:** is the right fix to *exempt the built-in* or to *narrow the detector*? Narrowing is usually correct and fixes the class — but check the narrowing does not silently drop a real case (here, "windings differ" would have missed hole/hole double-subtraction, so the rule became "skip only when BOTH are outer"). swept 2026-08-11 **S194**, hits: 1, clean streak: 0 — **ACTIVE**

- **JSON-LD ↔ visible-content parity** (**UN-RETIRED 2026-08-08, S190** — retired at S64, re-check ownership moved A2→Pass L at S142, and L's 5th run found it recurred): an `application/ld+json` FAQ/HowTo/ItemList claim that no longer describes the shipped tool. **Detection, as narrowed by S190:** a hit is (a) a **closed enumeration** that asserts the complete set of something the UI has since grown ("one per image, a full sheet, or an existing font file" vs the wizard's four sources), or (b) a description of **how a feature works** that no longer describes it (the dashboard's "assign a preset and an end time to each period" vs the weekly grid). *Merely incomplete prose is still NOT a hit* — that part of S142's convention stands. **Always check the VISIBLE twin**: every claim on these pages has an on-page FAQ counterpart, and S190 found all three twins carrying the identical stale wording in EN and HE, so a JSON-LD-only fix would create a new mismatch. Swept 2026-08-08 (S190), **hits: 3** (font-maker, dashboard, dictionary — all fixed 3237da8), clean streak: **0** — ACTIVE. Re-checked in Pass L. Named unswept surface for the next L: `index.html`'s `ItemList` of 8 tools, the 7 `WebApplication` blocks' `featureList` where present, and the generator/flash-cards/torah/trope FAQ+HowTo blocks (S174 hand-verified flash-cards; the rest were checked under the OLD non-enumeration convention and deserve a pass under the narrowed one). **⚑ SWEPT 2026-08-13 (S201, 6th L) — that named surface is now covered, and it held the hits: 2 LIVE mismatches + 7 stale closed enumerations, all one concern** (the 2026-07-23 dictionary theme launch was half-propagated: the CSV FAQ answer + the JSON-LD HowTo step got "theme"; the JSON-LD FAQ answer, the visible HowTo step, the static fallbacks, the meta/og/twitter/WebApp/HowTo descriptions and the index ItemList + card did not — three different states on one answer). **Fixes GATE-2 APPROVED (all 12 sites, wording locked) — queued as S202's first fix; clean streak stays 0 until it ships and re-verifies.** generator/flash-cards/torah/trope claims: CLEAN under the narrowed convention; `featureList` exists on none of the 7 WebApplication blocks. NEW verification rule from this sweep: a parity byte check must cover head copy + visible twins + CSV rows together, and a NEW claim goes into both sides in one commit with identical wording (parity-by-construction — da22334). **⚑ S202 (2026-08-13): both live mismatches CLOSED (0d4373a — all 12 approved sites, insertion-only, pairs re-verified agreeing) — the S190-named unswept surface is now both swept (S201) and fixed (S202), so the next L run starts its clean-streak count from a complete baseline. Streak: 0.** **⚑ SWEPT 2026-08-15 (S216, 7th L) — 1 HIT, fixed in-session (6fdf370 + be6afe3); streak stays 0.** The hit is squarely the registered (a) shape: `torah_trainer.html` carries THREE closed enumerations of what the tool does (`WebApplication.description`, FAQ answer 1, and a five-step HowTo ending at "Project fullscreen") and the UI has since grown two whole take-away capabilities — a Copy panel with 26 authored `torah.copy.*` keys, and designed printed sheets — that the entire crawler-facing corpus never mentioned (copy 0 / clipboard 0 / print 0 / paste 0 across 818 chars of meta + 5,121 of ld+json). **NEW detection rule, learned the hard way this run: measure the right CORPUS.** Two parity tables contradicted each other because one sliced "everything before `</head>`" — on this page 88,641 chars, nearly all `<style>` — and scored 62 `print` hits that were CSS comments plus a `media="print"` font preload. Crawler-facing copy is exactly `<title>`, the `content=` of description/og:*/twitter:*, and the ld+json bodies; nothing else counts. **AND the S190 visible-twin rule bit the fix itself**: `6fdf370` moved the JSON-LD from 7 Questions to 8 while the page's `<details>` FAQ stayed at 7, re-opening the pattern in the act of closing it — caught only by re-reading this line at close-out, and closed by `be6afe3`. Treat "did I move the twin?" as a mandatory post-condition of any fix to this pattern, not a pre-condition of finding it. **Also swept and CLEAN this run:** the inverse direction over the 8 capabilities shipped since S201 (9 ships-but-never-claims gaps found across 12 pages × 2 capabilities; only the torah one is substantive — the rest are small affordances like copying a share code, deliberately not claimed). **⚑ SWEPT 2026-08-19 (S229, 8th L) — 1 HIT, fixed in-session; streak stays 0.** The hit is the registered (a) shape again and in the same file S190 first found it: `Hebrew_Font_Maker.html`'s `WebApplication.description` enumerates the input paths as "from your handwriting — trace letters, place nikkud and trop, and export…", while the SAME page's HowTo step 1 and its "How do I make my own Hebrew font?" FAQ answer both already say a letter can be "drawn right in the browser". Draw mode is not new — it is one of three parallel claims that went stale while its two siblings were updated, which is precisely why the twin rule exists. **The (a) arm was otherwise the widest ever run on this pattern and came back clean: 1,037 crawler-visible strings → 109 numeric/closed-list claims → 10 falsifiable ones verified against the code, all true** (7-step tour, 26 marks, 10 questions, three drill kinds, 54 parshiyot, font cap 10, 13,081 words behind "over 13,000", 0–9999, and resources' 4 age groups + 6 categories). **The inverse direction was also swept: 6 of 8 capabilities shipped since S216 are claimed; the 2 that are not (FM stroke replay, trope missed-marks review) are sub-affordances of claimed capabilities and are correctly unclaimed** — the same call S216 made. **NEW detection rule from this run, and it is about the DENOMINATOR: verify a generated artefact's coverage independently of its own freshness check.** `llms.txt`/`llms-full.txt` now carry this pattern's claims into a second file; `update-llms-txt.mjs --check` only proves the file matches what the generator would emit today, so a regressed JSON-LD block round-trips clean. Counting the emitted steps/questions (38/47) against a per-page inventory of the source blocks is what actually closes that gap. **Named surface for the next L:** `featureList` still exists on none of the 8 WebApplication/CollectionPage blocks (unchanged since S201), and `index.html`'s `@graph` ItemList of 8 tools has not been re-verified against the tool pages' own descriptions since S201.

- **wired-then-clobbered label** (NEW, registered S192): an element that carries a **correct `data-i18n` binding** and is then **overwritten by a JS setter with a hardcoded English literal** — so `applyStaticI18n` translates it and the setter immediately reverts it. Distinct from `pre-ready-i18n / never-re-rendered` (a builder that runs before `I18n.ready` and is never re-run): here the key IS referenced and the wiring IS correct; a later writer clobbers it. **Why both gates are blind to it:** the literals characteristically sit in a **ternary** (`c ? 'Edit kern class' : 'New kern class'`) or an **array** rather than a plain assignment, which is exactly Check A's documented blind spot; and Check B only measures CSV translation coverage, which is complete. **Detection (repeatable, cheap):** build a map of `id → data-i18n key` from the file's static markup, then scan every `.textContent`/`.innerHTML`/`.value`/`.placeholder` assignment whose RHS contains an English string literal and no `I18n.t(`, resolving the target element by the nearest preceding `getElementById` within ~12 lines. **Triage rule learned on the first run:** that ID-proximity heuristic mismatches — 2 of 4 raw candidates were the generator's printed worksheet subtitles attributed to an unrelated `worksheet.layout.title_aria` binding, and printed output is never-translate anyway, so **always confirm the resolved element really is the bound one before logging**. **Fix shape:** retarget the binding as well as the text (`setAttribute('data-i18n', k)` + `textContent = I18n.t(k)`) — the existing suite idiom at `flash_cards.html` `timerShowLabel`. That is what makes a language switch land, and it avoids the trap of "just add the function to `applyI18n`", which is **illegal** when the function mutates state (`applyI18n` must stay read-only). Guard the text write against the pre-ready case (`t()` returns the key before locales load) so a raw dot-key can never be painted. Swept 2026-08-11 (S192, first sweep): **4 raw / 2 real / 2 fixed / 0 left**, across all 13 root HTML files. Clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE.

- **theme-flipping-token-on-a-fixed-colour-plate** (NEW, registered S191): a control or text node styled with a colour token that **inverts with the theme** — `var(--text)`, `var(--white)`, `var(--muted)` — placed inside a container painted a **fixed** colour that does not invert (a `--navy`/`--navy-deep` plate, a gold button, a print sheet). One theme composites fine and the other collapses toward 1:1, so a single-theme check clears it and the failure lands in whichever theme the author was not looking at. **This is the documented `--white` pitfall in CLAUDE.md read in the other direction** — that note warns `var(--white)` text disappears on navy in DARK; the S191 hit was `var(--text)` disappearing on navy in **LIGHT** (the bulk dock's `.btn-secondary`, measured 1:1, label rendered as an empty box). **Detection is not greppable** — the token and the plate are in different rules — so it needs the alpha-compositing contrast probe run in **both** themes, with transparent backgrounds walked up to an opaque ancestor. The house fix is the existing navy-plate idiom: literal `#fff` on `rgba(255,255,255,0.12)`. **Consequence-critical (a control whose label is invisible), so it does not retire on a clean streak.** — ACTIVE **2nd sweep 2026-08-11 (S193 Pass A): 1 hit, fixed (cd52e15).** Clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE. **Definition widened: the class has a MIRROR IMAGE** — S191's was an inverting token on a fixed plate; trope_tutor's is a **fixed** colour (the UA default `#0000EE` on an anchor no rule reached) on a plate that **inverts**. Same failure and same 1–2:1 floor, opposite cause; the compositing detector finds both because it measures the result, not the tokens. Detail + the new one-evaluate sub-detector in the sweep log below. **⚑ S194: 1 more hit on a NEW carrier via the S193 UA-default-anchor detector** — the Font Maker's 3 `.hint` anchors (`#0000EE`, **1.81:1** on the dark Advanced panel), fixed 01ebdb5 with the same `--gold-text` one-liner. That makes **3 carriers in 4 sessions** (torah_trainer dock, trope_tutor About, FM hints) and confirms the detector's value: it is one page-evaluate, needs no compositing baseline, and the misses are always anchors the page simply never styled because a `footer a`/`.panel a` rule did not reach them. **Next carriers to sweep: the 5 dormant anchors the S193 run found un-rendered** — enable each one's disclosure state first, which is exactly what turned the FM hint links from "never measured" into a confirmed 1.81:1. **Re-swept 2026-08-12 (S199) via the UA-default-anchor sub-detector, with every disclosure FORCED OPEN so the dormant carriers render: 1 hit (index `.ie-note a`, 1.63:1 dark, fixed 071e326) + 1 REFUTED.** That closes the "5 dormant anchors" queue and the count reconciles exactly: 3 FM hint links (S194) + these 2. **Standing false positive, do not re-chase:** `hebrew_dictionary .skip-results` reads 1.81:1 in dark but only while clipped to 1×1px offscreen; its only visible state is `:focus`, which sets `background:var(--navy); color:#fff`. **A forced-open detector must be paired with a real-state confirmation** — the index hit was re-measured with the gear modal genuinely opened before it was logged. **S202 hit (the mirror image again): the FM wizard modal's `.tbtn.ghost` — a fixed navy-toolbar token (gold-light) on the theme-flipping modal plate — 1.5:1 in light on the gate's only exit; fixed 3a33b1a by rescoping the file's own `.tour-card` repair. Sub-shape family now: inverting-token-on-fixed-plate (S191), UA-anchor-on-inverting-plate (S193/S199), fixed-token-on-inverting-plate (S193 trope, S202 FM).** **Swept again 2026-08-29 (S285 Pass C, `hebrew_dictionary`): 2 HITS, both fixed** (`f5b8c1e` the `.tip-icon` help badge 6.15 light → **3.05** dark; `5e748d3` the generator's `[DEFAULT]` marker **4.13** dark, the twin of the `.font-opt-attr` lift S225 already shipped). Clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE. **Definition widened again by S285 with two sub-shapes worth naming, because both defeat the plain probe:** (1) **the FILLED-BADGE inversion** — the plate itself is the theme-flipping token (`background:var(--muted)`) under FIXED ink (`color:#fff`), i.e. the mirror of the S191 shape with the roles swapped; a probe that only looks for a flipping *foreground* on a fixed plate misses it entirely. (2) **the INLINE-STYLE carrier** — the generator's marker had been failing since S225 *specifically because* it was written as an inline `style="color:var(--muted)"`, which no `body.dark` rule can override, so the sibling's fix could not reach it; **a fix for this class must check whether the carrier is inline, or it will silently not apply.** **And the plate, not the token, decides:** the `[DEFAULT]` markup is byte-identical on all 6 font-picker carriers and fails on exactly 2 (generator + dictionary, both 4.13) while the other 4 land 5.81–9.78 — so this class must be swept **per carrier**, never inferred from source.

- **two-state-ready-flag-for-a-three-state-load** (NEW, registered S189): a lazily-fetched corpus or module whose UI decides what to render from a single truthiness check — `REAL_WORDS.length`, `EMOJI_DATA`, `_wordsReady`. **That flag has two states; the fetch has three** (never attempted / in flight / failed), so the "not ready" arm is also what a FAILED load renders, permanently: either a confident false zero ("0 matching words" — worse than silence, because it is a claim about the user's own selection) or a "Loading…" that never ends, refreshed by every later re-render and language switch. **Detection:** for each lazy fetch, name its ready flag, grep every render that branches on it, and ask what the failure path leaves on screen; then stall the resource AND 502 it headless, reading the end state **after ≥4 s** — a short sample cannot tell "stuck" from "not yet". **Run both languages:** the dictionary instance PASSED in English and FAILED in Hebrew, because the later locale fetch changes whether a re-render lands after the catch. Also check whether the FIRST write happens *before* the fetch exists — the generator's guard was correct and still never fired, because every trigger path painted the caption before calling the loader (fix at the loader, not the call site). Swept 2026-08-08 (S189, Pass F) over the primary slow operation of all 7 tools, **hits: 3 of 7** (generator, flash cards, dictionary — the last with a twin instance two lines away in the same function), **all fixed same-session**; clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE. **Unswept sibling surfaces named for the next A:** the four transliteration-ESM status lines (`#translitLoadStatus` in generator/flash cards/dictionary, `#optTranslitStatus` in torah), the dashboard's `fetchShabbat`, and torah_trainer's `manifestData`/`parshiyotData` loads. **Re-swept 2026-08-11 (S193 Pass A): CLEAN — all 3 S189 hits fixed, three-state idiom now in place. Clean streak: 1 — ACTIVE.**

- **invalid-SVG-geometry-from-an-unclamped-difference** (NEW, registered S187): an SVG `width`/`height` computed as the difference of two mapped coordinates (`fx(b) - fx(a)`, `x1 - x0`) where one side comes from a **derived** value that can legitimately go negative — so the attribute goes negative, and per spec the browser **does not render the element at all** and logs an error. The overlay silently disappears in exactly the unusual case it was there to explain, and the console error repeats on every render. **Sibling-asymmetry is the tell:** one of a paired accessor clamps (`letterRSB` → `Math.max(0, …)`) and the other forgot to (`letterLSB`). **Detection:** wrap the `innerHTML` setter and regex added markup for `<rect[^>]*(?:width|height)="-` — the raw console count UNDERSTATES the frequency because Chromium collapses repeated identical messages (measured S187: 4 real assignments, 1 console line). Then check every `width="${…}"` built as a difference. **Swept 2026-08-08 (S187) over Hebrew_Font_Maker's 21 rect emitters: 1 hit (`marginGuidesSVG`'s left zone, fixed 74e0530, + the identical `wideFormGuidesSVG` shape guarded), rest clean** — `node-marquee` uses `Math.abs`, `markSelectRect` clamps to MIN 22, the capture-box rect was measured positive, and the handle/point rects are fixed-size. **Not yet swept elsewhere** — the obvious carriers are the generator's worksheet cut-line/QR geometry and torah_trainer's trope-underline print rules. clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE. **Re-swept 2026-08-11 (S193 Pass A): CLEAN — and both named carriers emit ZERO `<rect>`, so the shape is Font-Maker-only in practice. Clean streak: 1 — ACTIVE.**

- **RTL-inheritance-on-a-Latin-script-container**: **re-swept 2026-08-29 (S290 iter 4, `hebrew_dictionary.html` word cards) — hits: 1 carrier (`.wc-transl` + `.wc-translit`), fixed `21538fc`; clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE.** **4th carrier of the shape registered at S185, and the biggest population yet: 2,296 of 13,081 corpus entries** end in a period that rendered at the visual START, plus 139 apostrophe-leading transliterations. **Detection refinement:** the tell is a Latin-script container with no `direction`/`unicode-bidi` inside an RTL ancestor **whose content begins or ends with a NEUTRAL** (period, apostrophe, parenthesis, bracket) — the neutral is what visibly migrates; purely alphabetic Latin content inherits RTL harmlessly and is NOT a hit. **Fix shape now settled — use this, do not re-derive:** `unicode-bidi:plaintext` for ORDER (per-line, so genuinely Hebrew-first strings still order RTL; a blanket `direction:ltr` is wrong for those) **+ a `[dir="rtl"]`-SCOPED physical `text-align` for POSITION**, because under plaintext `start`/`end` follow each line's own resolved direction. **⚑ Scope the alignment pin or you regress the ENGLISH UI** — an unscoped pin moved the dictionary's EN glosses left→right, caught only by measuring both UIs on a SHORT string (a full-width line is flush to both edges and cannot discriminate alignment). _(registered S185: a container whose CONTENT is Latin script — an English translation, a transliteration, a Latin-labelled readout — that declares no `direction`, so under the Hebrew UI (`<html dir="rtl">`) it inherits an RTL base direction and every sentence-final period, comma or bracket jumps to the wrong end. Silent in the English UI, silent to `check-i18n` (nothing is untranslated), and it reaches PAPER as well as screen. **Detection:** render each layout in the HE UI and compare `getComputedStyle(el).direction` against the script of the text the element actually carries; assert under `emulateMedia({media:'print'})` too. **⚠ DETECTION AMENDED S187 — the computed-`direction` test alone OVER-REPORTS badly.** Swept over trope_tutor (the tool the S186 pointer named as the unswept carrier): **29 Latin-carrying leaves all compute `direction:rtl`, and per-character `Range` x-position comparison in EN vs HE found 0 of 7 punctuated strings visually reordered** — a single uninterrupted LTR run keeps logical order under an RTL base regardless (bracket pairs included, BD16). So the **mandatory second stage is a visual-order comparison**; a hit requires punctuation that can actually move, which in practice means **sentence-final** punctuation at the END of the run (what the real f5a0d72 hit had), not punctuation enclosed inside it. Counting computed-direction alone would have manufactured 29 false hits here. **Swept 2026-08-06 (S185) over torah_trainer's three reading layouts: 1 hit (side-by-side's two Latin columns, fixed f5a0d72), 2 clean** — interlinear pins `.tt-translit`/`.tt-translation` itself and Page view carries `dir="ltr"` on its bible blocks. **Not yet swept anywhere else** — the obvious carriers are the generator's worksheet/answer-key transliteration cells, flash-cards' card faces, and the dictionary's English/transliteration rows, all of which render Latin content inside a page that flips to `dir="rtl"`. **Pin on the ROW/cell, not the column**: a column-level pin also flips translated `<h3>` chrome, which is a regression (measured S185 — the drafted one-liner in the S181 candidate would have done exactly that). **trope_tutor swept CLEAN 2026-08-08 (S187), screen AND print.** clean streak: 1 — ACTIVE.)

- **silent-external-media-failure** (an `<audio>`/`<video>`/media element pointed at a third-party host with play/pause/ended handlers wired but **no `error` handler**, so a blocked or dead origin produces silence while the controls still show a live playing state. Detection: answer the media URL with an error response — `route.abort()` leaves the element STALLED rather than errored, so it never fires — and drive the real play path, because a `preload="none"` element fetches nothing until `play()`. Any control still reading "stop"/"pause" afterwards is a hit.) — **registered + first swept 2026-08-02 (S183)** on `torah_trainer.html` only: **1 hit** (the PocketTorah MP3, fixed a6bf328), clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE. **Unswept elsewhere:** the trope tutor's `#tuAudio` clip engine plays the same PocketTorah MP3s and has its own `_badFiles`/`onError` path that should be checked against this definition, and the dashboard's YouTube iframe is a third-party media embed with no error surface at all. **Swept 2026-08-08 (S187) over trope_tutor's `#tuAudio` clip engine — the surface the S186 pointer named as the unswept carrier: CLEAN, and MEASURED rather than read.** Per S183's method note the MP3 was fulfilled with a **502** (an `abort` leaves the element stalled, not errored): `MediaError.code 4`, `_badFiles.size 2`, a visible localized `role="status"` line "Audio unavailable right now — check your connection.", 0 pageerror. `playClip` carries a per-load `error` listener **and** a 20 s timeout for the black-holed-network case the pattern names, plus a token guard and seek verification — the reference implementation for this class.

- **print-trailing-dead-space** (padding/margin BELOW the last line of a print flow — page-container bottom padding, a scroll wrapper's, the last block's own margin — which paginates exactly like content, so a document ending near a page boundary pushes empty box onto a sheet of its own. Detection: under `emulateMedia({media:'print'})` at the true printable width, compare the page container's `getBoundingClientRect().bottom` against the deepest bottom edge of any text-bearing descendant; any positive delta is dead space that can cost a sheet. Confirm on real PDFs, never on emulation alone.) — **re-swept 2026-08-15 (S219) across ALL 12 root pages — the S182 coverage gap is CLOSED: 1 hit (`flash_cards.html`, 114px of leading dead space from an un-hidden `main.wrap`, fixed 4bfdd55), 11 clean**, clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE. **Detection was BROADENED in S219 and the new form supersedes the old one:** S182's method compared a page container's bottom edge against its deepest text-bearing descendant, which by construction can only see *trailing* space — and the S219 hit was *leading* (an emptied wrapper sitting above the flow). Use instead: under print media, any VISIBLE element ≥40px tall with no visible text and no `img/svg/canvas/hr` beneath it is empty box on paper; report outermost-first so one chain is not listed repeatedly. Keep S182's container-bottom check as a second arm. **Two paper-specific traps, both mandatory:** (1) confirm on real PDFs with REAL margins — `page.pdf()` defaults to margin 0, at which the S219 hit measured 16/16 clean and at 1in measured 16/16 broken; (2) if the page tears its print artifact down on `afterprint`, `page.pdf()` fires that event, so re-build the artifact before every render or the second measurement is of an empty document. Prior run: registered + first swept 2026-08-02 (S182) on `torah_trainer.html` only, 1 hit (22–44px, fixed 6896ba5). **Remaining coverage note:** the 11 clean pages were swept in their DEFAULT print state; a page whose artifact requires an explicit mode (as flash-cards' three do) is only as swept as the modes that were entered — the generator's worksheet and the dashboard's schedule sheet were each measured in one state.

- **lazily-loaded-dependency-renders-an-empty-shell** (a feature whose data comes from a lazily-loaded external module keeps rendering its full chrome — column, header, row label, legend — when the module never arrives, so the user gets a labelled void with the toggle still reading ON. Detection: block the module's origin at the network layer and render every layout that consumes it; any surviving header/label with no content is a hit. Note the failure is invisible in normal testing because the CDN is always up.) — **registered + first swept 2026-08-02 (S182)** on `torah_trainer.html` only: **1 hit** (the esm.sh transliterator, fixed af90983), clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE. Sibling surfaces not yet checked: the generator + flash-cards + dictionary transliteration paths (same esm.sh module), Font Maker's pyodide/harfbuzz/opentype loads, and the dashboard's Hebcal/weather widgets.

- **print-media-leak / var-chain-overridden-by-a-literal** (a screen-only `@media (max-width:N)` block whose declarations also apply to PAPER — print media has a width too — or, more generally, a literal `font-size`/colour declaration that out-specifies a `var(--x)` chain the UI's own controls feed. Detection: for every `@media (max-width:` block, ask whether it is qualified with `screen`, and diff its declared properties against the properties any `var(--…)`-driven rule sets on the same selectors; then compute the printable content width for Letter and A4 at each margin preset (Letter 816/768/740/624px, A4 794/746/**718**/602px at none/minimum/default/1in) and check which blocks fire. **A4 at default margins is 718px — under any 720px breakpoint** — which is why this is invisible to anyone testing on Letter): swept 2026-08-02 (S181), hits: **1 (fixed ce1eab2)**, clean streak: 0 — **ACTIVE**. Second instance of the var-chain half in two sessions: S180's `body.fullscreen` hardcoded `font-size` over the same `--tt-heb-size` chain (b7b7b7a). Consequence-critical-adjacent: it silently corrupts the printed artifact a student receives, so it does NOT retire on a clean streak alone.

- **incomplete-print-token-reset** (a `@media print` dark-token re-statement that restates SOME of the theme tokens the dark block overrides but not all — the missing ones keep their dark values on paper. Detection: diff the token list inside the print block's `html.dark-early body, body.dark { … }` against the full set the page's dark block defines, then check each missing token's consumers for `color:` on light paper or `background:` on a print-visible element. Note a *surface* token must take the light PAPER value, not its light-theme value): swept 2026-08-02 (S181), hits: **2 tokens in 1 file (fixed a4c581d)**, clean streak: 0 — **ACTIVE**. Not yet swept across the other 5 pages that carry a print block — standing backlog for the next A or G.

KEPT ACTIVE (the class recurs whenever a lookup ships before its rows; the sweep is one command).** **Re-swept S177 (2026-07-31) over d734fa6..HEAD: 0 of 175 newly-referenced keys missing (dynamic prefixes expanded first — raw first-args give 79 false misses); clean streak 2. Runtime cross-check: 24/24 page-language loads, 0 missing-key warnings, collector sanity-proven.** **Re-swept S179 (2026-08-01, Pass A): CLEAN, clean streak 3 — KEPT ACTIVE** (the class recurs whenever a lookup ships before its rows). Detector upgraded again and worth reusing: `/js/i18n.js` served through a `page.route` fulfill with a recorder injected into `t()`, logging every (key, resolved, dictLoaded, lang), counting a miss ONLY when `dictLoaded=1` — pre-ready misses are the runtime's own suppressed window, not a gap. Surface ~104 page loads: 12 pages × {EN, HE-via-?lang=he, EN-then-live-switch}, plus 10 pages × EN/HE driven through every collapsible panel (incl. the FM trop panel that hid the founding 28).

- **untrusted-shape-on-read** (a store that arrives from an imported `.ivrit` / AllTools file — hand-editable text — is read back with its SHAPE assumed: `results.map`, `(r.cards||[]).forEach`, `results.slice().reverse()`. - **parse-per-call on a growing store** (a `read<Store>()` helper that re-parses its whole localStorage blob on every call, called O(n) times per render, over a store that grows without bound as the teacher uses the tool — so the tool punishes use, and the cost is invisible at the small sizes a developer tests with): **registered + swept 2026-07-29 (S170, Pass D), hits: 1 of 4 candidate stores** — `readProfiles()` in flash_cards (9→47 calls per render, 408 ms→10.6 s; fixed 6ff3a0a). **Detection:** for each `read*()` that wraps `ivritSafeParse(localStorage.getItem(...))`, instrument it to count calls during one render at 1×, then re-measure with a synthetic store at realistic classroom scale (not 1 item). A store that is read more than ~3× per render OR whose blob can exceed ~100 KB is a hit. **Not yet swept:** `readPresets()` (flash_cards/generator/dashboard), `ftRead()` (5 folder keys, all tiny), `ivritSuite_wordLists` (dictionary/flash_cards), `hebrewTropeTutor_progress`. Clean streak: 0 — KEPT ACTIVE (a freeze that scales with a teacher's saved work reads as data loss). **Re-swept 2026-08-01 (S179, Pass A) — the ledger's own 'sweep them in the next A' list, done: 2 hits, 2 clean.** HITS: `getSettings()` in BOTH flash_cards and the generator re-parses the whole `ivritSuite_wordLists` blob once per selected list (`wlGetListName` → `wlReadStoreLocal` → reviver-based `ivritSafeParse`), unconditional and undebounced; measured linear scaling at 30×60 (184 KB) and the app's own ceiling 50×200 (1,031 KB). CLEAN: `readPresets()` (all three tools) and `ftRead()` (5 tiny trees). Logged as P3, not fixed this session. Clean streak: 0 — KEPT ACTIVE. **FIRST FIX 2026-08-06 (S184): the generator + flash-cards `getSettings()` arm closed (1f5b9c2) via `wlNamesForIds` — one store read per call instead of one per selected list, with an empty-set early return so the no-lists case still costs zero parses. - **authored-but-unreferenced i18n key family** (a `*.<family>.*` group that exists in `ui-strings.csv`, is fully translated, and is referenced **nowhere** in the page that owns it — so a Hebrew-UI user sees English while the translation sits in the repo. Costs nothing to fix and is **invisible to both check-i18n gates**: Check A only sees plain-literal assignments and static markup, Check B only checks that keys *have* translations, never that anything *uses* them): **registered 2026-07-29 (S170)** — retroactively covers S166's `fontmaker.ad.*` (14 keys) and S167's letter/vowel names (66). **Swept S170, hits: 5 families/sites** — `dashboard.glyphname.*` (13 keys, fixed ba73f0a), torah `loop_pause_label`+`_tip` and `trope.about.reset_all` (fixed 7aff49f), and ~~still open: `flashcards.glyphname.*` (45 keys) + `flashcards.teachertools.panel_title`~~ (closed S172 dc51fe6). **Swept + fixed again S173 (6th–7th instances, both FM):** 21 keys 29883a8 (metrics/forms/combined-nav/kern) + the 8-key `mark_*` family b2897b3; FM census now **91 remaining** (top candidate carries the breakdown). **Detection (cheap and reliable):** for each family prefix in the CSV, `grep -c "<prefix>" <owning page>` — a 0 is a hit; then confirm by measuring (set the UI to Hebrew and read the control chrome). **S175 (10th instance): the copy-blocked trio resolved via the answered gate batch (4c8f3c1); census 66 counted / ~54 true.** **Swept + fixed again S174 (8th–9th instances, both FM): 28 more keys/params live (9b37441 + 273d6d7), 4 more CSV markup restores; census 91→67 counted but ~55 TRUE — the file now HAS dynamic key construction (`anchorLabelT`), so subtract dynamically-referenced keys AND the 7 known authored-duplicates.** **S173 method correction for FM specifically: expand the `_pT`/`_cgT`/`_adT` prefixing helpers before counting** — suffix-referenced keys never appear as full strings (a naive scan overcounted 146 vs the true 120). Clean streak: 0 — KEPT ACTIVE (it recurs every time a key batch is authored ahead of its wiring, which is the suite's normal workflow). **Re-swept S177 via full census (arithmetic corrected: 33 true-unwired, 19 placeholder-normalized duplicates): 14 wired (49e9147), 20 CSV rows deleted (20ff25e) — 18 remain in FM (combined:6, place-panel:5, drop-zones:4, form-intros:3), families + code sites recorded in the S177 probe output. ACTIVE.** **Re-swept 2026-08-01 (S179, Pass A): 5 NEW families/sites, all logged** — FM QA modal (17 of 21 `fontmaker.qa.*`), the entire 30-key `fontmaker.canvas.*` family (0 repo-wide occurrences), torah's 13 `torah.glyphname.vowel_*`, flash_cards' 9 `flashcards.vowelgroup.color_*`, and FM `traced_readout`. All fully translated ⇒ 0 new copy to wire. **Detector matured:** literal `t()`/`data-i18n*` + DEPTH-AWARE first-arg extraction (resolves ternaries like `t(x?'a.one':'a.other')` — worth 6 false positives before it was added) + automatic prefixing-helper discovery and call-site expansion (`_pT`, `_cgT`, `_adT`/`_adTB`, `fcGlyphName`). It also re-derived the open FM census as **23 true-unwired, not 18**. Clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE. **Re-swept 2026-08-11 (S193 Pass A) with S192's runtime detector: 27 hits, 0 NEW — the count fell from 35 by exactly the two families S192 fixed, which is this method's first stability receipt. 1 family fixed this session (the dictionary's 9 vowel sub-labels, 05a0112). Clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE.** **2 more instances fixed 2026-08-13 (S200), AT THE 2/PATTERN SESSION CAP:** flash_cards' `flashcards.vowelgroup.color_*` (c6c6c04 — 7 group headers read "צליל AH – Aqua") and torah_trainer's `torah.glyphname.vowel_*` + `trope_*` (849e312 — 13 vowel rows, 6 trope rows, and 13 half-Hebrew aria-labels), both from the S179 Pass A list, both zero-new-copy. **Two fix-shape notes for the next instance, because neither was a key swap:** (1) **check what the English literal is DOING before replacing it** — flash-cards' English carries a teaching mnemonic (`<u>A</u>qua` = "A for AH") that a naive swap silently deletes; the generator's `vowelColorLabel` already solved it by using the translation only when it differs from the English word, so converge on that rather than inventing. (2) **do not assume the CSV slug is a slugify of the display name** — torah's three hataf rows ("H. Patach" → `h_patach`) miss their `hpatach` key, so map from the stable `def.key` explicitly, the shape the generator's `VOWEL_SUB_KEY` already documents. **Also: read the CSV `context` column before scoping** — torah's trope keys say "legend + picker label", which is what proved the picker was always an intended consumer and made fixing both lists one concern rather than two. **S205: the S179 five-family haul is fully closed (qa+traced_readout S204 670ba01, canvas S205 39282c9, torah/flash_cards S200); next sweep starts from a clean slate.**

- **sub-floor touch target on a shared small-button class** (NEW, registered S193): a small-control class — `.btn-xs` and its kin — whose size comes from `padding` **alone**, so its rendered height lands below the suite's ratified **30px** floor (WCAG 2.5.8 asks 24px). Because the class is shared, one missing rule puts **every** small button in that tool under the bar at once, which is why this is a class and not a per-button candidate. **Detection (no judgement calls):** headless per page, both themes × desktop/narrow, all panels/drawers open, collect `getBoundingClientRect()` for every `.btn-xs` and count `height < 30` and `height < 24`. **The fix is a copy, not an invention:** flash_cards' S102 declarations — `min-height`/`min-width:30px` plus `display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center`, where the inline-flex is what turns the min-height into a taller **box** instead of taller text. **Two guards are mandatory afterwards**, because a min-height reflows tight rows: horizontal page overflow (`scrollWidth - clientWidth`) must not move, and no target may overflow a clipping ancestor. **Swept + fixed 2026-08-11 (S193): 44 rendered targets across 4 files, 44 under 30px, 14 under 24px → all 44 at 30px, overflow unchanged at 0, 0 clipped (97a16b7).** History: S102 set the floor in flash_cards, S178 brought its remainder + the shared folder-tree, S193 closed the other four carriers — **3 sessions, 6 files, same shape**, which is what earns it a registry line. **Remaining surface is everything that is NOT `.btn-xs`** (torah_trainer's candidate still names ~50 such controls). Clean streak: 0 — ACTIVE. **⚑ S194 WIDENS THE CLASS PAST `.btn-xs`:** torah_trainer's `.slider-row .sreset` (5 buttons, **24×21**) is the same shape under a different class name — size from `padding` alone, no `min-height`/`min-width` — so the pattern is *any* small-control class sized by padding, not the `.btn-xs` family specifically. Fixed 0164489 with the identical declarations `.btn-xs` already carries in that same file. **Detection lesson, and it is the important half:** a naive `min(w,h) < 30` census over `button,a,input,select,[role=button]` **overcounts badly** — it returned 59 (S191) then 31 (S194) for the same page, and the majority were **0×0 visually-hidden checkboxes** whose styled label is the real hit area and **4px range-slider tracks** whose thumb is draggable. Exclude those two shapes plus `.tip-*`/`.vh-file`/running-text links **before** reporting any number. swept 2026-08-11 **S194**, hits: 1 (new class), clean streak: 0 — **ACTIVE** **⚑ CENSUS CLOSED 2026-08-12 (S196):** the last known member — the shared `.i18n-select` language switcher in `js/i18n.js`, 26.2px on all 12 pages — was brought to 30.0px (32b09be), completing the sweep S193 (`.btn-xs`, 5 files) → S194 (`.sreset`) → S195 (torah_trainer's four `<select>`s) → S196 started. **0 known members remain**; a future one would have to be newly introduced, so this stays ACTIVE as a cheap re-sweep rather than retiring. Note the shared-runtime case needed its own iteration precisely because one rule there moves every page at once — verify suite-wide (S196 used 24 measurement cells + a 36-cell reflow guard at 1280/800/420). **RE-OPENED 2026-08-13 (S200) — the S196 "census CLOSED, 0 known members left" note was true only of `.btn-xs`.** hebrew_dictionary's `.pos-all-btn` is a second shared small-button class of the same shape (height from `padding` alone), and it rendered 10 of its 12 buttons at 20–22px: **the first instance found under WCAG 2.5.8's 24px, not merely under the house 30px floor** (f4b5751, 40/48 → 0/48 sub-floor). **Definition widened accordingly: the class is "a shared small-control class sized by padding alone", NOT "`.btn-xs`" — detect by measuring every small control's rendered height, not by grepping one class name.** The mandatory guards held again (page overflow unchanged, no clipping-ancestor overflow) and a third is now recommended: confirm the taller box does not clip its own label, **in Hebrew as well as English**, since Hebrew labels are the longer ones. **S201 adds two more carriers** (both queued by the S178 haul, both shipped): hebrew_dictionary `.cb-label` — 57 rows, 39 under 24px at 19.2px, height from `line-height` alone (the class's first non-button member) → `min-height:24px` + 16×16 input (387a6a1); and the `.font-size-row input[type=range]` twins in dictionary + generator — **a new sub-shape: an explicit `height:4px` shrinks the OPERABLE box while the native thumb overflows it and looks grabbable** — 6 sliders → 24px with the visual provably unchanged via element screenshots (3ae6891). Detection widened again: measure every small control's rendered box — padding-only sizing AND explicit tiny heights both belong to the class. Remaining named surface: the non-`.font-size-row` sliders (generator `#zoomSlider` 16px; dashboard `.size-row` + FM `.inline`/`.zoom-bar` unmeasured — candidate logged) and the S178 haul's residue. **S202 (FM census, measured-not-fixed, appended to the range-slider candidate): `.side-slider`/`#zoomRange` 16px, `#drawSmoothingSel` 19px, `.chk` rows 21px; FM carries no `.btn-xs` — its buttons/tiles all cleared the 24px census at desktop and take 44px at ≤820px via the coarse-pointer arm.** **2nd sweep 2026-08-13 (S203 Pass A): 1 hit** — the FM Edit-points contours rows (`.ct-name`/`.ct-eye`/`.ct-del` ~19–21px, a carrier outside the S193 `.btn-xs` census; destructive ✕ in the mis-tap zone), **fixed in-session 1410e7b** at S193's 30px shape. FM's other small-control classes remain un-censused — a future arm, not a clean bill. **S236 (Pass C, dashboard): the class-scoped detection has a BLIND SPOT — class-less inline-styled small buttons.** The zoom-bar Reset (18px) and weather ↺ Refresh (19px) predate `.btn-xs` and carry their own inline padding, so the S193 `.btn-xs`-scoped sweep could never see them; both fixed by giving them the class (3a7cee4, inline look preserved). - **ivrit-gather-gap** — **3rd fix landed 2026-08-06 (S185)**: flash_cards' `hebrewFlashCards_pbStreak`, absent from BOTH of the tool's save paths and from `apply()`, now round-trips with AllTools' max rule (94d1222).
